author: Pipa
title: El viaje de Pipa
summary: Pipa leaves his design desk for the Americas, but a message from Argentina gives his journey a new purpose: finding the courage to answer in Spanish.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Mi lápiz dibuja una chaqueta, pero yo miro el mapa.
sentences.english: My pencil draws a jacket, but I am looking at the map.

sentences.spanish: Soy Pipa, un lagarto que diseña ropa en una oficina.
sentences.english: I am Pipa, a lizard who designs clothes in an office.

sentences.spanish: Junto al café tengo una mochila y un cuaderno vacío.
sentences.english: Beside my coffee I have a backpack and an empty notebook.

sentences.spanish: Hoy cierro la puerta y empieza mi viaje por América.
sentences.english: Today I close the door and my journey across the Americas begins.

sentences.spanish: En México llego a Puerto Escondido y escribo junto al mar.
sentences.english: In Mexico I arrive in Puerto Escondido and write beside the sea.

sentences.spanish: Quiero contar mis aventuras, pero todavía me faltan palabras.
sentences.english: I want to tell people about my adventures, but I still lack the words.

continuation.spanish: De Tabasco sigo hacia Guatemala y Belice.
continuation.english: From Tabasco I continue towards Guatemala and Belize.

continuation.spanish: En Costa Rica una mosca aterriza en mi desayuno; soy un lagarto con suerte.
continuation.english: In Costa Rica a fly lands on my breakfast; I am a lucky lizard.

continuation.spanish: Después de Perú llego a Colombia con muchos nombres en mi cuaderno.
continuation.english: After Peru I reach Colombia with many names in my notebook.

continuation.spanish: Allí enseño inglés y mis nuevos amigos me enseñan español.
continuation.english: There I teach English and my new friends teach me Spanish.

continuation.spanish: Tenemos dos chats de WhatsApp: uno en inglés y otro en español.
continuation.english: We have two WhatsApp chats: one in English and the other in Spanish.

continuation.spanish: Entonces llega un mensaje de Argentina: «¿Nos cuentas tu viaje cuando llegues?».
continuation.english: Then a message arrives from Argentina: “Will you tell us about your journey when you arrive?”

ending.spanish: Mi avión sale mañana y todavía tengo miedo de hablar.
ending.english: My plane leaves tomorrow and I am still afraid to speak.

ending.spanish: Escribo una respuesta en español, la borro y respiro.
ending.english: I write a reply in Spanish, erase it and breathe.

ending.spanish: Mi amiga dice: «No necesitamos una historia perfecta; queremos tu historia».
ending.english: My friend says, “We do not need a perfect story; we want your story.”

ending.spanish: Grabo un mensaje sobre una oficina, un café y una mochila.
ending.english: I record a message about an office, a coffee and a backpack.

ending.spanish: Desde Argentina llegan risas y una pregunta: «¿Y después?».
ending.english: From Argentina come laughter and a question: “And then?”

ending.spanish: Sonrío y vuelvo a grabar; esta vez tengo mucho que contar.
ending.english: I smile and record again; this time I have a lot to tell.

author: Musgo
title: La puerta bajo las raíces
summary: A whisper under Musgo’s garden leads to his father’s forgotten spell, and a door that should never have been left shut.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Mi padre deja una llave negra debajo de una maceta.
sentences.english: My father leaves a black key beneath a flowerpot.

sentences.spanish: «Es para el jardín», dice, pero el jardín no tiene puerta.
sentences.english: “It is for the garden,” he says, but the garden has no gate.

sentences.spanish: Por la noche oigo mi nombre bajo la tierra.
sentences.english: At night I hear my name beneath the soil.

sentences.spanish: Soy Musgo y conozco muchos hechizos, pero esta voz no es mía.
sentences.english: I am Musgo and I know many spells, but this voice is not mine.

sentences.spanish: Aparto las hojas y encuentro una cerradura entre las raíces.
sentences.english: I move the leaves aside and find a lock among the roots.

sentences.spanish: La llave está caliente en mi mano.
sentences.english: The key is warm in my hand.

continuation.spanish: Abro la puerta y sale una sombra pequeña.
continuation.english: I open the door and a small shadow comes out.

continuation.spanish: Tiene los ojos de mi padre y un sombrero de hojas.
continuation.english: It has my father’s eyes and a hat made of leaves.

continuation.spanish: «Tengo sed», dice la sombra.
continuation.english: “I am thirsty,” says the shadow.

continuation.spanish: Busco mi libro de magia oscura y una vela.
continuation.english: I fetch my book of dark magic and a candle.

continuation.spanish: La sombra sopla la vela y señala la regadera.
continuation.english: The shadow blows out the candle and points to the watering can.

continuation.spanish: Por primera vez esta noche, sé qué hacer.
continuation.english: For the first time tonight, I know what to do.

ending.spanish: Doy agua a las raíces y la sombra crece.
ending.english: I water the roots and the shadow grows.

ending.spanish: Ahora veo flores dentro de su cuerpo negro.
ending.english: Now I can see flowers inside its black body.

ending.spanish: Mi padre llega con dos tazas de té.
ending.english: My father arrives with two cups of tea.

ending.spanish: «Es mi primer hechizo; cuida este lugar cuando yo no estoy».
ending.english: “It is my first spell; it looks after this place when I am away.”

ending.spanish: Dejo la puerta abierta y pongo la llave en mi bolsillo.
ending.english: I leave the door open and put the key in my pocket.

ending.spanish: A la mañana siguiente, alguien ha regado mis plantas.
ending.english: The following morning, someone has watered my plants.

author: Pipa
title: El billete de vuelta
summary: On the last train home, Pipa finds a ticket that belongs to someone who has been waiting much longer than he has.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Compré el último billete y subí al tren con la bufanda mojada.
sentences.english: I bought the last ticket and boarded the train with my scarf wet.

sentences.spanish: Después de tantos viajes, por fin volvía a casa.
sentences.english: After so many journeys, I was finally going home.

sentences.spanish: En mi asiento había un sobre con mi nombre.
sentences.english: On my seat there was an envelope with my name on it.

sentences.spanish: Dentro encontré un billete antiguo y una fotografía de mi abuela.
sentences.english: Inside I found an old ticket and a photograph of my grandmother.

sentences.spanish: En la foto llevaba mi misma mochila, pero parecía nueva.
sentences.english: In the photograph she was carrying my very backpack, but it looked new.

sentences.spanish: Al otro lado del pasillo, una anciana me observaba.
sentences.english: On the other side of the aisle, an elderly woman was watching me.

continuation.spanish: «Tu abuela me pidió que te lo diera», dijo.
continuation.english: “Your grandmother asked me to give it to you,” she said.

continuation.spanish: Las dos habían planeado cruzar las montañas cuando eran jóvenes.
continuation.english: The two of them had planned to cross the mountains when they were young.

continuation.spanish: Mi abuela perdió el tren porque su madre estaba enferma.
continuation.english: My grandmother missed the train because her mother was ill.

continuation.spanish: Su amiga hizo el viaje sola y guardó los dos billetes.
continuation.english: Her friend made the journey alone and kept both tickets.

continuation.spanish: «Siempre dice que irá el año que viene», añadió la anciana.
continuation.english: “She always says she will go next year,” the elderly woman added.

continuation.spanish: Miré mi calendario lleno de lugares y dejé una página en blanco.
continuation.english: I looked at my calendar full of places and left one page blank.

ending.spanish: Mi abuela nos esperaba en la estación con una bolsa de pan.
ending.english: My grandmother was waiting for us at the station with a bag of bread.

ending.spanish: Al ver a su amiga, dejó caer la bolsa y abrió los brazos.
ending.english: When she saw her friend, she dropped the bag and opened her arms.

ending.spanish: Yo recogí el pan mientras ellas hablaban las dos a la vez.
ending.english: I picked up the bread while they both talked at once.

ending.spanish: Durante la cena les enseñé tres billetes para el sábado.
ending.english: During dinner I showed them three tickets for Saturday.

ending.spanish: «Esta vez llevo yo la mochila», dijo mi abuela.
ending.english: “This time I am carrying the backpack,” my grandmother said.

ending.spanish: No conocía aquel camino, pero ya sabía con quién quería recorrerlo.
ending.english: I did not know that route, but I already knew whom I wanted to travel it with.

author: Zumi
title: Un barco para una mosca
summary: Zumi’s wings cannot carry him through the rain, and the first passenger on his experimental boat is a creature who cannot swim.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Yo sabía volar, pero no sabía nadar.
sentences.english: I knew how to fly, but I did not know how to swim.

sentences.spanish: Por eso todos se rieron cuando construí un barco con una nuez.
sentences.english: That was why everyone laughed when I built a boat from a walnut.

sentences.spanish: «Para los días de lluvia», expliqué, colocando una hoja como vela.
sentences.english: “For rainy days,” I explained, putting a leaf in place as a sail.

sentences.spanish: Aquella tarde la lluvia llegó antes de la prueba.
sentences.english: That afternoon the rain arrived before the test.

sentences.spanish: Al otro lado de un charco, una hormiga gritaba sobre una piedra.
sentences.english: On the other side of a puddle, an ant was shouting from a stone.

sentences.spanish: El agua ya le llegaba a los pies.
sentences.english: The water was already reaching her feet.

continuation.spanish: Intenté volar hasta ella, pero las gotas me golpeaban las alas.
continuation.english: I tried to fly to her, but the drops were hitting my wings.

continuation.spanish: Volví a la orilla y empujé mi pequeño barco.
continuation.english: I returned to the bank and pushed my little boat out.

continuation.spanish: La vela se cayó inmediatamente; nadie se rio esta vez.
continuation.english: The sail fell down immediately; nobody laughed this time.

continuation.spanish: Usé un palito como remo y avancé muy despacio.
continuation.english: I used a little stick as an oar and moved forward very slowly.

continuation.spanish: «¡No saltes todavía!», grité al acercarme a la piedra.
continuation.english: “Do not jump yet!” I shouted as I approached the stone.

continuation.spanish: La hormiga puso una pata dentro y el barco se inclinó.
continuation.english: The ant put one leg inside and the boat tilted.

ending.spanish: Me moví al otro extremo y la nuez recuperó el equilibrio.
ending.english: I moved to the other end and the walnut regained its balance.

ending.spanish: Remamos juntos hasta tocar el barro de la orilla.
ending.english: We rowed together until we touched the mud on the bank.

ending.spanish: Mi pasajera bajó, temblando, y me devolvió el remo.
ending.english: My passenger got out, trembling, and returned the oar to me.

ending.spanish: «Mañana necesito cruzar otra vez», dijo.
ending.english: “Tomorrow I need to cross again,” she said.

ending.spanish: En mi cuaderno escribí: «Dos remos, ninguna vela».
ending.english: In my notebook I wrote: “Two oars, no sail.”

ending.spanish: Todavía no sabía nadar, pero ahora tenía una compañera de pruebas.
ending.english: I still did not know how to swim, but now I had a testing partner.

author: Luma
title: La luz del observatorio
summary: Luma climbs the hill to investigate a light in an abandoned observatory and discovers why its keeper refuses to let it go out.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La luz apareció en el observatorio una noche sin luna.
sentences.english: The light appeared in the observatory on a moonless night.

sentences.spanish: Llevaba años viendo aquellas ventanas vacías desde mi calle.
sentences.english: I had been looking at those empty windows from my street for years.

sentences.spanish: Me dijeron que una polilla prudente no debía acercarse.
sentences.english: I was told that a sensible moth should not go near it.

sentences.spanish: Sin embargo, alguien había encendido una lámpara y luego la había tapado tres veces.
sentences.english: However, someone had lit a lamp and then covered it three times.

sentences.spanish: No parecía una invitación, sino una llamada de ayuda.
sentences.english: It did not look like an invitation, but a call for help.

sentences.spanish: Guardé unas cerillas junto al té y emprendí la subida.
sentences.english: I packed some matches beside the tea and began the climb.

continuation.spanish: Encontré al viejo guardián sentado bajo un telescopio roto.
continuation.english: I found the old keeper sitting beneath a broken telescope.

continuation.spanish: Un temporal había arrancado el cable del teléfono y bloqueado la puerta exterior.
continuation.english: A storm had torn down the telephone cable and blocked the outer door.

continuation.spanish: Yo había entrado por una ventana demasiado estrecha para él.
continuation.english: I had entered through a window too narrow for him.

continuation.spanish: La lámpara era su última señal, pero apenas quedaba aceite.
continuation.english: The lamp was his last signal, but there was hardly any oil left.

continuation.spanish: Podía volver al pueblo, aunque la niebla ya ocultaba el camino.
continuation.english: I could return to the village, although the fog was already hiding the path.

continuation.spanish: Entonces vi los espejos que antes dirigían la luz hacia el telescopio.
continuation.english: Then I saw the mirrors that had once directed light towards the telescope.

ending.spanish: Mientras él sostenía mi linterna, orienté los espejos hacia el valle.
ending.english: While he held my lantern, I angled the mirrors towards the valley.

ending.spanish: La señal cruzó la niebla y alcanzó las ventanas de la panadería.
ending.english: The signal crossed the fog and reached the bakery windows.

ending.spanish: Poco después, unas voces contestaron desde la ladera.
ending.english: Shortly afterwards, voices answered from the hillside.

ending.spanish: Cuando nos abrieron la puerta, el guardián llevaba dos tazas en las manos.
ending.english: When they opened the door for us, the keeper was holding two cups.

ending.spanish: «Pensé que vendría alguien más grande», confesó.
ending.english: “I thought someone bigger would come,” he confessed.

ending.spanish: Le serví el té: aquella noche una ventana pequeña había sido suficiente.
ending.english: I poured him some tea: that night a small window had been enough.

author: Brasa
title: La campana sin voz
summary: Brasa has one hour to repair the village bell before the fog hides the returning fishing boats.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La campana del puerto no suena.
sentences.english: The harbour bell does not ring.

sentences.spanish: Yo tengo una hora y una caja de herramientas.
sentences.english: I have one hour and a toolbox.

sentences.spanish: Después llega la niebla y los barcos necesitan escucharla.
sentences.english: Afterwards the fog arrives and the boats need to hear it.

sentences.spanish: Subo a la torre con mis alas pequeñas.
sentences.english: I climb the tower with my small wings.

sentences.spanish: Dentro hay un nido, tres huevos y una cuerda rota.
sentences.english: Inside there is a nest, three eggs and a broken rope.

sentences.spanish: No puedo mover el nido; la madre me mira.
sentences.english: I cannot move the nest; the mother is watching me.

continuation.spanish: Pido una cuerda nueva por la ventana.
continuation.english: I ask for a new rope through the window.

continuation.spanish: Abajo, Tilo trae una cuerda demasiado corta.
continuation.english: Below, Tilo brings a rope that is too short.

continuation.spanish: La niebla ya cubre el primer barco.
continuation.english: The fog already covers the first boat.

continuation.spanish: Pongo mi bufanda junto a la cuerda.
continuation.english: I put my scarf beside the rope.

continuation.spanish: Tilo entiende y busca más bufandas en el café.
continuation.english: Tilo understands and looks for more scarves in the café.

continuation.spanish: Pronto tenemos una cuerda de todos los colores.
continuation.english: Soon we have a rope of every colour.

ending.spanish: Paso la cuerda lejos del nido y tiro.
ending.english: I pass the rope away from the nest and pull.

ending.spanish: La campana suena sobre el agua blanca.
ending.english: The bell rings over the white water.

ending.spanish: Un barco responde con su propia campana.
ending.english: A boat answers with its own bell.

ending.spanish: Después llega otro, y después otro más.
ending.english: Then another arrives, and then another one.

ending.spanish: Bajo al café sin bufanda, pero nadie tiene frío.
ending.english: I go down to the café without a scarf, but nobody is cold.

ending.spanish: En la torre, tres huevos descansan junto a nuestro arcoíris.
ending.english: In the tower, three eggs rest beside our rainbow.

author: Tilo
title: El cuaderno de los favores
summary: Tilo discovers that someone has removed every name from the village’s book of favours, just when he needs to ask for help.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: El cuaderno estaba abierto sobre mi mesa, pero sus páginas habían perdido todos los nombres.
sentences.english: The notebook lay open on my table, but its pages had lost every name.

sentences.spanish: Durante años había anotado allí los favores que nos hacíamos en el pueblo.
sentences.english: For years I had recorded the favours we did for one another in it.

sentences.spanish: Ahora necesitaba ayuda para trasladar nuestro pequeño teatro antes de la crecida.
sentences.english: Now I needed help moving our little theatre before the flood.

sentences.spanish: Sin aquellas notas, no sabía a quién me correspondía llamar.
sentences.english: Without those notes, I did not know whose turn it was to help me.

sentences.spanish: Una mancha de tinta avanzó sola hacia el borde del papel.
sentences.english: An ink stain moved by itself towards the edge of the paper.

sentences.spanish: Fui a buscar a Musgo con el cuaderno apretado contra mi caparazón.
sentences.english: I went to find Musgo with the notebook pressed against my shell.

continuation.spanish: Musgo reconoció el frasco que yo había usado para rellenar mi pluma.
continuation.english: Musgo recognised the bottle I had used to refill my pen.

continuation.spanish: Era tinta para borrar deudas, no tinta para escribir recuerdos.
continuation.english: It was ink for erasing debts, not ink for writing memories.

continuation.spanish: Le pedí que deshiciera el hechizo, pero necesitaba una noche entera.
continuation.english: I asked him to undo the spell, but he needed a whole night.

continuation.spanish: El río no iba a esperar tanto.
continuation.english: The river was not going to wait that long.

continuation.spanish: Salí a la plaza y pedí ayuda sin mencionar ninguna deuda.
continuation.english: I went out into the square and asked for help without mentioning any debt.

continuation.spanish: Durante unos segundos solo se oyó el agua bajo el puente.
continuation.english: For a few seconds, only the water beneath the bridge could be heard.

ending.spanish: Luego llegó la panadera con su carro y el barquero con dos cuerdas.
ending.english: Then the baker arrived with her cart and the boatman with two ropes.

ending.spanish: Otros vecinos levantaron los bancos mientras yo recogía los títeres.
ending.english: Other neighbours lifted the benches while I gathered the puppets.

ending.spanish: Cuando el río alcanzó la puerta, la última cortina ya estaba a salvo.
ending.english: When the river reached the door, the last curtain was already safe.

ending.spanish: Musgo me preguntó si todavía quería recuperar los nombres.
ending.english: Musgo asked whether I still wanted to recover the names.

ending.spanish: Le dije que sí, pero que esta vez no escribiría quién debía qué.
ending.english: I said yes, but that this time I would not write who owed what.

ending.spanish: Abrí una página limpia y puse el título de nuestra próxima obra: «La noche de todos».
ending.english: I opened a clean page and wrote the title of our next play: “Everyone’s Night.”

author: Pipa
title: El mapa de los errores
summary: Pipa’s carefully drawn guide sends everyone the wrong way, until one wrong turn reveals a place worth finding.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Dibujé un mapa del pueblo para los viajeros de la posada.
sentences.english: I drew a map of the village for the travellers at the inn.

sentences.spanish: Marqué la plaza, el puente y el mejor lugar para desayunar.
sentences.english: I marked the square, the bridge and the best place for breakfast.

sentences.spanish: Por la mañana, tres huéspedes volvieron cubiertos de barro.
sentences.english: In the morning, three guests returned covered in mud.

sentences.spanish: Habían seguido mi flecha hacia el café y terminado en un huerto.
sentences.english: They had followed my arrow towards the café and ended up in an orchard.

sentences.spanish: Mi cola había extendido la tinta antes de que se secara.
sentences.english: My tail had spread the ink before it dried.

sentences.spanish: Quise romper el mapa, pero una huésped me detuvo.
sentences.english: I wanted to tear up the map, but one guest stopped me.

continuation.spanish: «En el huerto hay una puerta azul», me contó.
continuation.english: “There is a blue door in the orchard,” she told me.

continuation.spanish: «Alguien estaba cantando detrás, aunque parecía no haber nadie».
continuation.english: “Someone was singing behind it, although nobody seemed to be there.”

continuation.spanish: La acompañé con un paño, mi cuaderno y muchas disculpas.
continuation.english: I went with her, carrying a cloth, my notebook and many apologies.

continuation.spanish: Detrás de la puerta encontramos a un anciano arreglando un piano.
continuation.english: Behind the door we found an old man repairing a piano.

continuation.spanish: Llevaba meses esperando una pieza que nadie sabía entregar allí.
continuation.english: He had been waiting for months for a part that nobody knew how to deliver there.

continuation.spanish: El paquete estaba en la posada, con una dirección incompleta.
continuation.english: The parcel was at the inn, with an incomplete address.

ending.spanish: Volvimos con la pieza y ayudamos a mover el piano al patio.
ending.english: We returned with the part and helped move the piano into the courtyard.

ending.spanish: Al atardecer, todos los huéspedes escucharon la primera canción.
ending.english: At sunset, all the guests listened to the first song.

ending.spanish: El anciano puso café sobre una mesa junto a los árboles.
ending.english: The old man put coffee on a table beside the trees.

ending.spanish: Corregí la flecha, pero conservé el camino del huerto.
ending.english: I corrected the arrow, but kept the orchard path.

ending.spanish: Ahora mi guía tenía un lugar que no aparecía en ningún otro mapa.
ending.english: Now my guide had a place that did not appear on any other map.

ending.spanish: Debajo escribí: «A veces merece la pena preguntar adónde lleva el error».
ending.english: Underneath I wrote: “Sometimes it is worth asking where the mistake leads.”

author: Nube
title: Tres caminos y una tormenta
summary: Three travellers shelter beneath Nube, each insisting on a different road, while the storm makes their decision for them.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Desde arriba vi a tres viajeros discutir en un cruce.
sentences.english: From above I saw three travellers arguing at a crossroads.

sentences.spanish: Cada uno sostenía un mapa distinto y señalaba un camino diferente.
sentences.english: Each held a different map and pointed to a different road.

sentences.spanish: Yo llevaba una tormenta dentro y necesitaba llegar al valle antes de soltarla.
sentences.english: I was carrying a storm inside me and needed to reach the valley before releasing it.

sentences.spanish: Les advertí de la lluvia, pero creyeron que mi trueno era una opinión más.
sentences.english: I warned them about the rain, but they thought my thunder was just another opinion.

sentences.spanish: Me acerqué tanto que sus sombreros se llenaron de niebla.
sentences.english: I moved so close that their hats filled with mist.

sentences.spanish: Por fin guardaron los mapas y me preguntaron qué había visto.
sentences.english: At last they put away their maps and asked what I had seen.

continuation.spanish: El primer camino terminaba en un puente que la riada se había llevado.
continuation.english: The first road ended at a bridge that the flood had swept away.

continuation.spanish: El segundo cruzaba una ladera donde las piedras seguían cayendo.
continuation.english: The second crossed a slope where stones were still falling.

continuation.spanish: No sabía adónde llevaba el tercero: los árboles me habían impedido verlo.
continuation.english: I did not know where the third led: the trees had prevented me from seeing it.

continuation.spanish: El viajero más joven propuso seguir el sonido de un rebaño.
continuation.english: The youngest traveller suggested following the sound of a flock.

continuation.spanish: Los otros protestaron, hasta que distinguimos una campana entre los truenos.
continuation.english: The others protested, until we made out a bell among the thunder.

continuation.spanish: Un pastor salió del bosque y nos hizo señas desde una senda estrecha.
continuation.english: A shepherd emerged from the forest and beckoned to us from a narrow path.

ending.spanish: Llegamos a su refugio justo cuando ya no pude contener la lluvia.
ending.english: We reached his shelter just when I could no longer hold back the rain.

ending.spanish: Me quedé sobre el tejado y llené sus depósitos vacíos.
ending.english: I stayed over the roof and filled his empty water tanks.

ending.spanish: Dentro, los viajeros extendieron los mapas alrededor de una olla caliente.
ending.english: Inside, the travellers spread their maps around a hot pot.

ending.spanish: Ninguno mostraba aquella senda, así que la dibujaron juntos.
ending.english: None showed that path, so they drew it together.

ending.spanish: Al amanecer, el pastor me agradeció el agua y ellos me enseñaron el nuevo mapa.
ending.english: At dawn, the shepherd thanked me for the water and they showed me the new map.

ending.spanish: Habían añadido una nube pequeña donde antes solo había un cruce.
ending.english: They had added a little cloud where there had previously been only a crossroads.

author: Mora
title: Las cartas sin nombre
summary: Mora drops three letters into a puddle and must find their owners using the mysterious objects inside.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Tengo tres cartas y ninguna tiene nombre.
sentences.english: I have three letters and none has a name.

sentences.spanish: Esta mañana caen en un charco desde mi cesta.
sentences.english: This morning they fall into a puddle from my basket.

sentences.spanish: El agua borra las direcciones, pero las cartas están secas por dentro.
sentences.english: The water erases the addresses, but the letters are dry inside.

sentences.spanish: Una lleva una pluma, otra una semilla y otra un botón.
sentences.english: One contains a feather, another a seed and another a button.

sentences.spanish: Antes de la fiesta tengo que encontrar a sus dueños.
sentences.english: Before the party I have to find their owners.

sentences.spanish: Mi primer intento es llevar la pluma a Faro.
sentences.english: My first attempt is to take the feather to Faro.

continuation.spanish: «No es mía», dice Faro; «es una pluma para escribir».
continuation.english: “It is not mine,” Faro says; “it is a writing quill.”

continuation.spanish: Musgo mira la semilla y niega con la cabeza.
continuation.english: Musgo looks at the seed and shakes his head.

continuation.spanish: Pipa tampoco conoce el botón rojo.
continuation.english: Pipa does not recognise the red button either.

continuation.spanish: Me siento en la plaza con las tres cartas.
continuation.english: I sit in the square with the three letters.

continuation.spanish: Tilo pasa con una chaqueta sin botón y un libro vacío.
continuation.english: Tilo passes by with a jacket missing a button and an empty book.

continuation.spanish: De su bolsillo sale una flor de papel.
continuation.english: A paper flower sticks out of his pocket.

ending.spanish: Las tres cartas son para Tilo.
ending.english: All three letters are for Tilo.

ending.spanish: Una amiga le manda una pluma para su nueva obra.
ending.english: A friend sends him a quill for his new play.

ending.spanish: Otra le manda una semilla para decorar el teatro.
ending.english: Another sends him a seed to decorate the theatre.

ending.spanish: Su hermana le manda el botón de su chaqueta.
ending.english: His sister sends him the button from his jacket.

ending.spanish: «¡Ya tengo mis regalos!», dice, y me invita a la fiesta.
ending.english: “Now I have my presents!” he says, and invites me to the party.

ending.spanish: En mi cesta pongo una tapa antes de salir.
ending.english: I put a lid on my basket before leaving.

author: Brasa
title: La lluvia sobre el escenario
summary: A storm threatens Brasa’s first performance, and his attempt to dry the roof creates a much bigger problem.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La noche de mi primera obra empezó con una gotera.
sentences.english: The night of my first play began with a leak.

sentences.spanish: Una gota cayó sobre la nariz del rey, que era Tilo con una corona de cartón.
sentences.english: A drop fell on the king’s nose; the king was Tilo wearing a cardboard crown.

sentences.spanish: El público levantó los pies mientras el agua cruzaba el suelo.
sentences.english: The audience lifted their feet as the water crossed the floor.

sentences.spanish: Subí al desván y soplé aire caliente sobre las tejas.
sentences.english: I climbed to the attic and blew warm air over the roof tiles.

sentences.spanish: Quería secarlas, pero derretí la cera que tapaba una grieta.
sentences.english: I wanted to dry them, but melted the wax plugging a crack.

sentences.spanish: La gotera se convirtió en una pequeña cascada.
sentences.english: The leak became a little waterfall.

continuation.spanish: Bajé al escenario preparado para pedir perdón.
continuation.english: I went down to the stage ready to apologise.

continuation.spanish: Tilo me miró y gritó: «¡El dragón ha abierto las puertas del mar!».
continuation.english: Tilo looked at me and shouted, “The dragon has opened the gates of the sea!”

continuation.spanish: Los niños empezaron a remar con los programas de papel.
continuation.english: The children started rowing with the paper programmes.

continuation.spanish: Comprendí la idea y arrastré un banco hasta el centro.
continuation.english: I understood the idea and dragged a bench to the centre.

continuation.spanish: «¡Todos al barco!», anuncié, mientras Mora repartía cubos.
continuation.english: “Everyone aboard!” I announced, while Mora handed out buckets.

continuation.spanish: Nunca habíamos ensayado aquella escena.
continuation.english: We had never rehearsed that scene.

ending.spanish: El público pasó los cubos hasta la puerta al ritmo de nuestra canción.
ending.english: The audience passed the buckets to the door in time with our song.

ending.spanish: Cuando dejó de llover, el suelo estaba casi seco.
ending.english: When it stopped raining, the floor was almost dry.

ending.spanish: Conté la verdad y prometí ayudar a reparar el tejado.
ending.english: I told the truth and promised to help repair the roof.

ending.spanish: La panadera ofreció tablas y el rey se quitó su corona mojada.
ending.english: The baker offered boards and the king removed his wet crown.

ending.spanish: Al día siguiente trabajamos hasta cerrar la última grieta.
ending.english: The next day we worked until we had sealed the last crack.

ending.spanish: Guardé un cubo en el teatro: no como herramienta, sino como recuerdo de nuestro primer éxito.
ending.english: I kept a bucket in the theatre: not as a tool, but as a reminder of our first success.

author: Faro
title: Los ojos al otro lado
englishTitle: The Eyes on the Other Side
summary: Faro and Benji investigate two glowing eyes beyond the farm fence, but the lookout notices something the owl has missed.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Llevaba una hora inmóvil sobre la cerca, vigilando dos luces entre los árboles.
sentences.english: I had been motionless on the fence for an hour, watching two lights among the trees.

sentences.spanish: Debajo de mí, Benji se escondía dentro de una bota abandonada.
sentences.english: Below me, Benji was hiding inside an abandoned boot.

sentences.spanish: Era un ratón, mi amigo y el mejor vigía de la granja.
sentences.english: He was a mouse, my friend and the best lookout on the farm.

sentences.spanish: Las luces aparecían cada noche después de que desapareciera un saco de grano.
sentences.english: The lights appeared every night after a sack of grain disappeared.

sentences.spanish: Todos hablaban de un monstruo; yo ya había escrito el título de su historia.
sentences.english: Everyone was talking about a monster; I had already written the title of its story.

sentences.spanish: Benji me pidió que no escribiera el final todavía.
sentences.english: Benji asked me not to write the ending yet.

continuation.spanish: Cuando las luces avanzaron, extendí las alas para lanzarme sobre ellas.
continuation.english: When the lights advanced, I spread my wings to swoop down on them.

continuation.spanish: Benji silbó desde la bota: había oído ruedas, no pasos.
continuation.english: Benji whistled from the boot: he had heard wheels, not footsteps.

continuation.spanish: Bajamos por lados distintos hasta rodear el camino.
continuation.english: We went down on different sides until we surrounded the path.

continuation.spanish: Las luces eran dos faroles sujetos al carro de una tejona.
continuation.english: The lights were two lanterns attached to a badger’s cart.

continuation.spanish: Llevaba el grano al molino porque el molinero se había roto una pierna.
continuation.english: She was taking the grain to the mill because the miller had broken a leg.

continuation.spanish: Había dejado notas, pero el viento las había arrancado de la puerta.
continuation.english: She had left notes, but the wind had torn them off the door.

ending.spanish: La acompañamos al molino y regresamos con harina para el desayuno.
ending.english: We accompanied her to the mill and returned with flour for breakfast.

ending.spanish: Alrededor del horno, conté lo que realmente habíamos descubierto.
ending.english: Around the oven, I told everyone what we had actually discovered.

ending.spanish: Me costó renunciar al monstruo, aunque Benji no tuvo la delicadeza de disimular su sonrisa.
ending.english: I found it hard to give up the monster, although Benji was not tactful enough to hide his smile.

ending.spanish: La tejona nos invitó a viajar con ella la noche siguiente.
ending.english: The badger invited us to travel with her the following night.

ending.spanish: Acepté y taché el título de mi cuaderno.
ending.english: I accepted and crossed out the title in my notebook.

ending.spanish: Debajo escribí: «El vigía que escuchaba lo que el búho no veía».
ending.english: Underneath I wrote: “The Lookout Who Heard What the Owl Could Not See.”

author: Pipa
title: Una costura antes del alba
summary: Pipa must repair a stranger’s torn coat before the morning bus, but a hidden pocket changes what the repair means.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La viajera llegó a la posada con un abrigo rasgado.
sentences.english: The traveller arrived at the inn with a torn coat.

sentences.spanish: Su autobús salía al amanecer y fuera empezaba a nevar.
sentences.english: Her bus left at dawn and outside it was beginning to snow.

sentences.spanish: Saqué mi pequeño costurero y le ofrecí una silla.
sentences.english: I took out my little sewing kit and offered her a chair.

sentences.spanish: Al abrir el forro, encontré un bolsillo cosido por dentro.
sentences.english: When I opened the lining, I found a pocket sewn on the inside.

sentences.spanish: Contenía una fotografía y un papel que decía: «Vuelve cuando quieras».
sentences.english: It contained a photograph and a piece of paper saying, “Come back whenever you like.”

sentences.spanish: La viajera dejó de mirar el reloj.
sentences.english: The traveller stopped looking at the clock.

continuation.spanish: Su madre había hecho aquel abrigo antes de su primer viaje.
continuation.english: Her mother had made that coat before her first journey.

continuation.spanish: Ella nunca había descubierto el bolsillo secreto.
continuation.english: She had never discovered the secret pocket.

continuation.spanish: Ahora llevaba meses buscando trabajo lejos de casa.
continuation.english: Now she had been looking for work far from home for months.

continuation.spanish: Mientras yo cosía, me preguntó si volver significaba fracasar.
continuation.english: While I sewed, she asked me whether going back meant failing.

continuation.spanish: Le conté que mi mochila siempre guardaba espacio para un billete de vuelta.
continuation.english: I told her that my backpack always had room for a return ticket.

continuation.spanish: No respondí por ella; terminé la manga y le devolví la fotografía.
continuation.english: I did not answer for her; I finished the sleeve and gave her back the photograph.

ending.spanish: Antes del alba bajó con un billete diferente.
ending.english: Before dawn she came downstairs with a different ticket.

ending.spanish: Había llamado a su madre y cambiado de destino.
ending.english: She had called her mother and changed her destination.

ending.spanish: Le enseñé dónde estaba el bolsillo y reforcé su borde.
ending.english: I showed her where the pocket was and reinforced its edge.

ending.spanish: En la puerta me pagó con una bufanda que había tejido durante sus viajes.
ending.english: At the door she paid me with a scarf she had knitted during her travels.

ending.spanish: La llevé al autobús y nos despedimos bajo la nieve.
ending.english: I took her to the bus and we said goodbye beneath the snow.

ending.spanish: Aquel día mi mejor trabajo fue una costura que nadie podía ver.
ending.english: That day my best work was a seam nobody could see.

author: Musgo
title: La habitación que no existía
englishTitle: The Room That Did Not Exist
summary: A forbidden spell gives Musgo an extra room, but each visit costs him a memory of the cottage he loves.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: El libro prometía una habitación nueva sin mover una sola pared.
sentences.english: The book promised a new room without moving a single wall.

sentences.spanish: Como mis plantas ya ocupaban la cocina, leí el hechizo en voz alta.
sentences.english: Since my plants already occupied the kitchen, I read the spell aloud.

sentences.spanish: Apareció una puerta negra donde antes colgaba el retrato de mi padre.
sentences.english: A black door appeared where my father’s portrait had hung.

sentences.spanish: Detrás había estanterías vacías y una ventana abierta a ninguna parte.
sentences.english: Behind it were empty shelves and a window opening onto nowhere.

sentences.spanish: Entré con mis libros, encantado con el resultado.
sentences.english: I went in with my books, delighted with the result.

sentences.spanish: Al salir, no recordaba quién había pintado el retrato.
sentences.english: When I came out, I could not remember who had painted the portrait.

continuation.spanish: Volví a entrar para consultar la letra pequeña del hechizo.
continuation.english: I went back in to consult the spell’s small print.

continuation.spanish: Cada visita entregaba un recuerdo a cambio de espacio.
continuation.english: Each visit surrendered a memory in exchange for space.

continuation.spanish: Quise deshacerlo, pero ya había olvidado dónde guardaba la tiza ritual.
continuation.english: I wanted to undo it, but I had already forgotten where I kept the ritual chalk.

continuation.spanish: Llamé a Faro y le pedí que me hablara de mi propia casa.
continuation.english: I called Faro and asked him to tell me about my own house.

continuation.spanish: Mientras describía nuestras cenas, las estanterías de la habitación empezaron a temblar.
continuation.english: As he described our dinners, the shelves in the room began to tremble.

continuation.spanish: Comprendí que los recuerdos compartidos no pertenecían solo a quien los perdía.
continuation.english: I understood that shared memories did not belong only to the person losing them.

ending.spanish: Invitamos a los vecinos y cada uno contó algo sucedido en la cocina.
ending.english: We invited the neighbours and each told of something that had happened in the kitchen.

ending.spanish: Con cada historia, un libro regresaba al suelo del pasillo.
ending.english: With each story, a book returned to the hallway floor.

ending.spanish: Cuando mi padre contó cómo había pintado su retrato, la puerta desapareció.
ending.english: When my father told how he had painted his portrait, the door disappeared.

ending.spanish: Me encontré rodeado de libros, macetas y personas que recordaba perfectamente.
ending.english: I found myself surrounded by books, flowerpots and people I remembered perfectly.

ending.spanish: Guardé el grimorio en una caja cerrada, con una advertencia sobre el precio.
ending.english: I put the grimoire in a locked box, with a warning about the price.

ending.spanish: La cocina seguía siendo pequeña, pero aquella noche cabíamos todos.
ending.english: The kitchen was still small, but that night there was room for everyone.

author: Mora
title: El precio de una historia
summary: Mora reaches the market where stories buy anything, only to discover that her favourite tale is not hers to sell.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: En este mercado una historia vale más que una moneda.
sentences.english: In this market a story is worth more than a coin.

sentences.spanish: Llego con mi cartera vacía y tres cuentos en la cabeza.
sentences.english: I arrive with an empty wallet and three tales in my head.

sentences.spanish: Quiero comprar un paraguas antes de la lluvia.
sentences.english: I want to buy an umbrella before the rain.

sentences.spanish: El vendedor pide mi mejor historia.
sentences.english: The seller asks for my best story.

sentences.spanish: Empiezo a contar un secreto de Faro.
sentences.english: I begin to tell one of Faro’s secrets.

sentences.spanish: Entonces veo al búho detrás del puesto.
sentences.english: Then I see the owl behind the stall.

continuation.spanish: Faro no dice nada, pero yo dejo de hablar.
continuation.english: Faro says nothing, but I stop speaking.

continuation.spanish: La historia no es mía y él no quiere contarla.
continuation.english: The story is not mine and he does not want to tell it.

continuation.spanish: El vendedor guarda el paraguas.
continuation.english: The seller puts the umbrella away.

continuation.spanish: Empieza a llover sobre mi sombrero de seta.
continuation.english: It begins to rain on my mushroom hat.

continuation.spanish: Faro se sienta a mi lado bajo una mesa.
continuation.english: Faro sits beside me beneath a table.

continuation.spanish: «Puedes contar lo que pasa ahora», dice.
continuation.english: “You can tell what is happening now,” he says.

ending.spanish: Cuento la historia de una mensajera con la cartera vacía.
ending.english: I tell the story of a messenger with an empty wallet.

ending.spanish: Quiere un paraguas y casi vende el secreto de un amigo.
ending.english: She wants an umbrella and almost sells a friend’s secret.

ending.spanish: Ahora está bajo una mesa y tiene mucha vergüenza.
ending.english: Now she is under a table and feels very ashamed.

ending.spanish: El vendedor escucha el final y me da el paraguas.
ending.english: The seller listens to the ending and gives me the umbrella.

ending.spanish: Es grande, con espacio para dos.
ending.english: It is large, with room for two.

ending.spanish: Faro y yo volvemos a casa sin vender ningún secreto.
ending.english: Faro and I return home without selling any secrets.

author: Brasa
title: La silla de la ventana
summary: Every guest avoids the empty chair in Brasa’s café, until a rain-soaked visitor recognises the name carved beneath it.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: En mi café nadie se sentaba en la silla de la ventana.
sentences.english: In my café nobody sat in the chair by the window.

sentences.spanish: Decían que pertenecía al capitán que no había vuelto del mar.
sentences.english: They said it belonged to the captain who had not returned from the sea.

sentences.spanish: Yo la limpiaba cada mañana y dejaba una taza delante.
sentences.english: I cleaned it every morning and left a cup in front of it.

sentences.spanish: Una tarde llegó una nutria con una maleta empapada.
sentences.english: One afternoon an otter arrived with a soaking suitcase.

sentences.spanish: Buscó un asiento, vio la silla y se quedó de pie.
sentences.english: She looked for a seat, saw the chair and remained standing.

sentences.spanish: Luego se agachó para leer algo debajo de la madera.
sentences.english: Then she bent down to read something beneath the wood.

continuation.spanish: El nombre grabado era el suyo.
continuation.english: The carved name was hers.

continuation.spanish: Su padre había prometido volver para enseñarle aquel café.
continuation.english: Her father had promised to return to show her that café.

continuation.spanish: Ella traía una carta que él había escrito en su último puerto.
continuation.english: She was carrying a letter he had written in his last port.

continuation.spanish: No pedía que reservaran su silla; pedía que recibieran bien a su hija.
continuation.english: He did not ask them to save his chair; he asked them to welcome his daughter.

continuation.spanish: Los clientes dejaron de hablar mientras ella doblaba el papel.
continuation.english: The customers stopped talking while she folded the paper.

continuation.spanish: Le pregunté cómo le gustaba el café.
continuation.english: I asked her how she liked her coffee.

ending.spanish: Se sentó junto a la ventana y abrió la maleta.
ending.english: She sat by the window and opened the suitcase.

ending.spanish: Dentro había cuadernos de viaje llenos de dibujos de su padre.
ending.english: Inside were travel notebooks full of her father’s drawings.

ending.spanish: Acercamos las mesas para poder verlos todos.
ending.english: We moved the tables closer so we could all see them.

ending.spanish: Ella contó historias que nadie en el pueblo conocía.
ending.english: She told stories that nobody in the village knew.

ending.spanish: Por la noche retiré la taza que siempre dejaba vacía.
ending.english: That night I removed the cup I always left empty.

ending.spanish: La silla tenía una nueva dueña y el café, una nueva amiga.
ending.english: The chair had a new owner and the café a new friend.

author: Mora
title: La moneda que volvía
summary: A strange coin follows Mora home after every purchase, bringing complaints from the entire market.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Compré una manzana y pagué con una moneda brillante.
sentences.english: I bought an apple and paid with a shiny coin.

sentences.spanish: Al llegar a casa, la moneda estaba otra vez en mi bolsillo.
sentences.english: When I got home, the coin was in my pocket again.

sentences.spanish: Pensé que había olvidado pagar y regresé al mercado.
sentences.english: I thought I had forgotten to pay and returned to the market.

sentences.spanish: La frutera me mostró su caja vacía.
sentences.english: The fruit seller showed me her empty till.

sentences.spanish: Le di la moneda, pero esta saltó sobre el mostrador y volvió hacia mí.
sentences.english: I gave her the coin, but it jumped over the counter and came back to me.

sentences.spanish: Reconocí en su borde una letra diminuta: la M de Musgo.
sentences.english: I recognised a tiny letter on its edge: Musgo’s M.

continuation.spanish: El mago había encantado la moneda para no perderla.
continuation.english: The wizard had enchanted the coin so he would not lose it.

continuation.spanish: Yo la había encontrado junto a su puerta y supuesto que era un regalo.
continuation.english: I had found it beside his door and assumed it was a gift.

continuation.spanish: «Solo vuelve al bolsillo que la guarda», explicó, buscando su libro.
continuation.english: “It only returns to the pocket that holds it,” he explained, looking for his book.

continuation.spanish: Probamos una cesta, un tarro y una caja cerrada.
continuation.english: We tried a basket, a jar and a locked box.

continuation.spanish: La moneda escapó de los tres y rompió el tarro.
continuation.english: The coin escaped from all three and broke the jar.

continuation.spanish: La frutera llegó justo cuando empezábamos a discutir con ella.
continuation.english: The fruit seller arrived just as we were beginning to argue with it.

ending.spanish: «No necesito vuestra moneda», dijo; «necesito que paguéis la manzana».
ending.english: “I do not need your coin,” she said; “I need you to pay for the apple.”

ending.spanish: Busqué una moneda corriente entre mis ahorros y se la entregué.
ending.english: I found an ordinary coin among my savings and handed it to her.

ending.spanish: Musgo se llevó la encantada dentro de mi bolsillo descosido.
ending.english: Musgo took the enchanted one away inside my unstitched pocket.

ending.spanish: A cambio, prometió coserme otro y reparar el tarro.
ending.english: In exchange, he promised to sew me another and repair the jar.

ending.spanish: La frutera volvió al mercado riéndose.
ending.english: The fruit seller returned to the market laughing.

ending.spanish: Yo terminé la manzana más cara y más viajera de mi vida.
ending.english: I finished the most expensive and most widely travelled apple of my life.

author: Brasa
title: La sopa del visitante
summary: An unexpected guest cannot eat Brasa’s famous Sunday soup, and the little dragon has to change more than his recipe.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Todos los domingos preparaba la misma sopa para mis vecinos.
sentences.english: Every Sunday I made the same soup for my neighbours.

sentences.spanish: Conocía la receta de memoria y me sentía bastante orgulloso.
sentences.english: I knew the recipe by heart and felt rather proud.

sentences.spanish: Aquel domingo apareció una visitante que solo comía plantas.
sentences.english: That Sunday a visitor appeared who ate only plants.

sentences.spanish: Miró la olla, sonrió con educación y pidió agua.
sentences.english: She looked at the pot, smiled politely and asked for water.

sentences.spanish: Yo había puesto caldo de carne en toda la sopa.
sentences.english: I had put meat stock in all the soup.

sentences.spanish: Por primera vez, mi gran mesa tenía un plato vacío.
sentences.english: For the first time, my big table had an empty plate.

continuation.spanish: Le ofrecí pan, pero apenas quedaba una corteza.
continuation.english: I offered her bread, but there was barely a crust left.

continuation.spanish: Quise salir a comprar algo, aunque las tiendas ya estaban cerradas.
continuation.english: I wanted to go and buy something, although the shops were already closed.

continuation.spanish: La visitante preguntó si podía mirar en mi huerto.
continuation.english: The visitor asked whether she could look in my vegetable patch.

continuation.spanish: Volvió con hierbas, un calabacín y una cebolla pequeña.
continuation.english: She returned with herbs, a courgette and a small onion.

continuation.spanish: Mientras cortábamos, los demás trajeron verduras de sus casas.
continuation.english: While we chopped, the others brought vegetables from their homes.

continuation.spanish: Mi segunda olla empezó a oler mejor que la primera.
continuation.english: My second pot began to smell better than the first.

ending.spanish: Servimos las dos sopas en el centro de la mesa.
ending.english: We served both soups in the middle of the table.

ending.spanish: La visitante nos enseñó a añadir las hierbas al final.
ending.english: The visitor taught us to add the herbs at the end.

ending.spanish: Anoté sus instrucciones en el margen de mi vieja receta.
ending.english: I wrote her instructions in the margin of my old recipe.

ending.spanish: Cuando pedimos repetir, su olla estaba casi vacía.
ending.english: When we asked for seconds, her pot was almost empty.

ending.spanish: La invité a volver el domingo siguiente y le pregunté qué le gustaría comer.
ending.english: I invited her back the following Sunday and asked what she would like to eat.

ending.spanish: Esta vez escuché la respuesta antes de encender el fuego.
ending.english: This time I listened to the answer before lighting the fire.

author: Tilo
title: La voz fuera de escena
summary: During Tilo’s silent film screening, an unseen voice starts correcting the story, and the audience demands to know who is speaking.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La película no tenía sonido, pero una voz interrumpió la primera escena.
sentences.english: The film had no sound, but a voice interrupted the first scene.

sentences.spanish: «Ese puente no estaba allí», dijo alguien al fondo del teatro.
sentences.english: “That bridge was not there,” someone said at the back of the theatre.

sentences.spanish: Yo había organizado la proyección de una vieja película sobre nuestro pueblo.
sentences.english: I had organised a screening of an old film about our village.

sentences.spanish: Al principio pedí silencio; después, la voz corrigió también el nombre de la estación.
sentences.english: At first I asked for silence; then the voice also corrected the station’s name.

sentences.spanish: El público empezó a murmurar y el proyector se atascó.
sentences.english: The audience began to murmur and the projector jammed.

sentences.spanish: Encendí las luces y encontré a una anciana junto a la salida.
sentences.english: I switched on the lights and found an elderly woman beside the exit.

continuation.spanish: Había trabajado en aquella estación antes de que la película se rodara.
continuation.english: She had worked at that station before the film was shot.

continuation.spanish: El director había cambiado los nombres y añadido un puente para simplificar la historia.
continuation.english: The director had changed the names and added a bridge to simplify the story.

continuation.spanish: «En la película, mi hermana parece la culpable de un accidente», explicó.
continuation.english: “In the film, my sister looks responsible for an accident,” she explained.

continuation.spanish: Le ofrecí una silla cerca de la pantalla y le pedí que contara su versión.
continuation.english: I offered her a chair near the screen and asked her to tell her version.

continuation.spanish: Otro vecino recordó una carta; una tercera persona trajo una fotografía.
continuation.english: Another neighbour remembered a letter; a third person brought a photograph.

continuation.spanish: Nuestra proyección se convirtió en una conversación que yo no podía dirigir.
continuation.english: Our screening became a conversation I could not direct.

ending.spanish: No resolvimos todos los desacuerdos aquella noche.
ending.english: We did not settle every disagreement that night.

ending.spanish: Sin embargo, escribimos qué mostraba la película y qué contaban los testigos.
ending.english: However, we wrote down what the film showed and what the witnesses said.

ending.spanish: La anciana aceptó volver para grabar sus recuerdos con su propio nombre.
ending.english: The elderly woman agreed to return to record her memories under her own name.

ending.spanish: Reparé el proyector y anuncié una segunda sesión.
ending.english: I repaired the projector and announced a second screening.

ending.spanish: Esta vez dejé una silla y un micrófono delante de la pantalla.
ending.english: This time I left a chair and a microphone in front of the screen.

ending.spanish: La historia del pueblo necesitaba más de una voz para poder contarse.
ending.english: The village’s story needed more than one voice to be told.

matchGlossary.contarse: to be told / to tell one another

author: Musgo
title: Las judías de medianoche
summary: Musgo’s enchanted beans climb towards a locked attic, but harvesting them means breaking a promise to his oldest neighbour.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Las judías crecieron durante la noche y atravesaron el techo de mi invernadero.
sentences.english: The beans grew during the night and pierced my greenhouse roof.

sentences.spanish: Había usado una gota de fertilizante y, por error, otra de un elixir prohibido.
sentences.english: I had used one drop of fertiliser and, by mistake, another of a forbidden elixir.

sentences.spanish: Al amanecer, sus tallos llegaban hasta el desván de la casa vecina.
sentences.english: At dawn, their stalks reached the attic of the neighbouring house.

sentences.spanish: La dueña me había hecho prometer que nunca abriría aquella ventana.
sentences.english: The owner had made me promise never to open that window.

sentences.spanish: Ahora las vainas golpeaban el cristal como dedos impacientes.
sentences.english: Now the pods were tapping on the glass like impatient fingers.

sentences.spanish: Dentro del desván, algo contestó con tres golpes.
sentences.english: Inside the attic, something answered with three knocks.

continuation.spanish: Fui a buscar a mi vecina en lugar de trepar a escondidas.
continuation.english: I went to find my neighbour instead of climbing up secretly.

continuation.spanish: Me contó que guardaba allí el violín de su hermano.
continuation.english: She told me she kept her brother’s violin there.

continuation.spanish: Desde su muerte no había querido oírlo ni permitir que nadie lo tocara.
continuation.english: Since his death she had not wanted to hear it or let anyone touch it.

continuation.spanish: Le expliqué que las plantas respondían a los sonidos que encontraban.
continuation.english: I explained that the plants responded to the sounds they found.

continuation.spanish: Ella escuchó los golpes y reconoció el principio de una canción.
continuation.english: She listened to the knocks and recognised the beginning of a song.

continuation.spanish: Después de un largo silencio, buscó la llave del desván.
continuation.english: After a long silence, she found the attic key.

ending.spanish: Subimos juntos y retiramos las ramas sin dañar el instrumento.
ending.english: We went up together and removed the branches without damaging the instrument.

ending.spanish: Mi vecina abrió el estuche, aunque decidió no tocar todavía.
ending.english: My neighbour opened the case, although she decided not to play yet.

ending.spanish: Esa decisión era suya, no de mis judías ni de mi magia.
ending.english: That decision was hers, not my beans’ or my magic’s.

ending.spanish: Deshice el hechizo y reparé el cristal con mis propias manos.
ending.english: I undid the spell and repaired the glass with my own hands.

ending.spanish: Una semana después, escuché una melodía desde la ventana abierta.
ending.english: A week later, I heard a melody from the open window.

ending.spanish: Seguí regando sin acercarme: algunas invitaciones no necesitan respuesta inmediata.
ending.english: I kept watering without going closer: some invitations do not need an immediate response.

author: Luma
title: Una luz para dos
summary: Luma prepares supper for a new neighbour, but an unanswered invitation leaves her following a trail of tiny lights.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Pongo dos platos en mi mesa por primera vez.
sentences.english: I put two plates on my table for the first time.

sentences.spanish: Mi nuevo vecino vive detrás del molino.
sentences.english: My new neighbour lives behind the mill.

sentences.spanish: Le dejo una invitación junto a su puerta.
sentences.english: I leave him an invitation beside his door.

sentences.spanish: A las ocho la sopa está caliente, pero él no llega.
sentences.english: At eight the soup is hot, but he does not arrive.

sentences.spanish: Desde mi ventana veo una luz pequeña cerca del río.
sentences.english: From my window I see a small light near the river.

sentences.spanish: Cojo mi farol y salgo a buscarlo.
sentences.english: I take my lantern and go out to look for him.

continuation.spanish: En el camino hay otra luz y después otra más.
continuation.english: On the path there is another light and then another one.

continuation.spanish: Son luciérnagas que esperan sobre las hojas.
continuation.english: They are fireflies waiting on the leaves.

continuation.spanish: Mi vecino está junto al puente con una pata atrapada.
continuation.english: My neighbour is beside the bridge with one leg trapped.

continuation.spanish: En la mano tiene flores para mi mesa.
continuation.english: In his hand he has flowers for my table.

continuation.spanish: No puedo mover la tabla sola.
continuation.english: I cannot move the plank alone.

continuation.spanish: Levanto el farol y llamo a los vecinos.
continuation.english: I raise the lantern and call the neighbours.

ending.spanish: Entre todos levantamos la tabla y lo ayudamos a salir.
ending.english: Together we lift the plank and help him get out.

ending.spanish: Volvemos despacio, con las luciérnagas delante.
ending.english: We return slowly, with the fireflies ahead.

ending.spanish: La sopa está fría y las flores están torcidas.
ending.english: The soup is cold and the flowers are bent.

ending.spanish: Caliento la olla y busco más platos.
ending.english: I heat the pot and look for more plates.

ending.spanish: Mi vecino pone las flores en un vaso.
ending.english: My neighbour puts the flowers in a glass.

ending.spanish: La cena para dos termina con seis sillas alrededor de la mesa.
ending.english: The dinner for two ends with six chairs around the table.

author: Tilo
title: El papel más pequeño
summary: Tilo promises everyone a place in his play, then discovers that one quiet volunteer does not want to be onstage at all.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Prometí que todos tendrían un papel en mi nueva obra.
sentences.english: I promised everyone a part in my new play.

sentences.spanish: Faro eligió al guardián y Brasa pidió ser el monstruo.
sentences.english: Faro chose the guard and Brasa asked to be the monster.

sentences.spanish: Luma llegó con una caja de luces y aceptó el papel de reina.
sentences.english: Luma arrived with a box of lights and accepted the part of the queen.

sentences.spanish: Durante el ensayo hablaba tan bajo que nadie podía oírla.
sentences.english: During rehearsal she spoke so quietly that nobody could hear her.

sentences.spanish: Le ofrecí un papel más pequeño, pero tampoco parecía contenta.
sentences.english: I offered her a smaller part, but she did not seem happy with that either.

sentences.spanish: Cuando terminó el ensayo, encontré su corona sobre una silla.
sentences.english: When rehearsal ended, I found her crown on a chair.

continuation.spanish: La busqué detrás del escenario, donde arreglaba una lámpara.
continuation.english: I looked for her backstage, where she was repairing a lamp.

continuation.spanish: Me dijo que había aceptado para no decepcionarme.
continuation.english: She told me she had agreed so as not to disappoint me.

continuation.spanish: No quería actuar; quería construir el cielo de la última escena.
continuation.english: She did not want to act; she wanted to build the sky for the final scene.

continuation.spanish: Yo había confundido ofrecer un lugar con elegirlo por ella.
continuation.english: I had confused offering a place with choosing it for her.

continuation.spanish: Le entregué los planos y dejamos la corona en su caja.
continuation.english: I handed her the plans and we left the crown in its box.

continuation.spanish: Los demás empezaron a ensayar sin ver qué preparaba.
continuation.english: The others began rehearsing without seeing what she was preparing.

ending.spanish: La noche del estreno, una tormenta de papel cubrió el escenario.
ending.english: On opening night, a paper storm covered the stage.

ending.spanish: Después, cientos de estrellas se encendieron sobre nuestras cabezas.
ending.english: Afterwards, hundreds of stars lit up above our heads.

ending.spanish: El público guardó silencio antes de aplaudir.
ending.english: The audience fell silent before applauding.

ending.spanish: Luma observaba desde un rincón, con la mano sobre el interruptor.
ending.english: Luma watched from a corner, with her hand on the switch.

ending.spanish: En el programa escribí su nombre junto a «Diseño del cielo».
ending.english: In the programme I wrote her name beside “Sky Design.”

ending.spanish: Era una línea pequeña para un trabajo que llenaba todo el teatro.
ending.english: It was a small line for work that filled the whole theatre.

author: Nube
title: Lo que cabe en una nube
summary: Nube gathers souvenirs from every village until the weight of his memories prevents him from leaving the ground.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Guardaba un recuerdo de cada pueblo en los bolsillos de mi abrigo.
sentences.english: I kept a souvenir from every village in my coat pockets.

sentences.spanish: Había llaves sin puerta, piedras de río y una campanilla que nunca sonaba.
sentences.english: There were keys without doors, river stones and a little bell that never rang.

sentences.spanish: Una mañana, el viento pasó y yo no conseguí levantarme del suelo.
sentences.english: One morning, the wind passed and I could not rise from the ground.

sentences.spanish: Me habían advertido que incluso una nube podía cargar demasiado.
sentences.english: I had been warned that even a cloud could carry too much.

sentences.spanish: Intenté elegir un objeto que no significara nada.
sentences.english: I tried to choose an object that meant nothing.

sentences.spanish: No encontré ninguno y perdí el viento que iba hacia el mar.
sentences.english: I found none and missed the wind that was heading towards the sea.

continuation.spanish: Pipa se sentó conmigo y me pidió la historia de la campanilla.
continuation.english: Pipa sat down with me and asked for the story of the little bell.

continuation.spanish: Pertenecía a un barquero que me había ayudado cuando una tormenta me desorientó.
continuation.english: It belonged to a boatman who had helped me when a storm disoriented me.

continuation.spanish: Al contarlo, recordé su risa con más claridad que al mirar el metal.
continuation.english: In telling it, I remembered his laugh more clearly than when looking at the metal.

continuation.spanish: Pipa dibujó la campanilla y me dio la página.
continuation.english: Pipa drew the little bell and gave me the page.

continuation.spanish: Pasamos la tarde escribiendo las historias de mis bolsillos.
continuation.english: We spent the afternoon writing the stories in my pockets.

continuation.spanish: Algunas ocuparon una línea; otras necesitaron varias hojas y una pausa.
continuation.english: Some occupied one line; others needed several pages and a pause.

ending.spanish: Dejé los objetos en la posada con una nota sobre cada uno.
ending.english: I left the objects at the inn with a note about each one.

ending.spanish: La posadera prometió abrir un pequeño rincón para los viajeros.
ending.english: The innkeeper promised to open a little corner for travellers.

ending.spanish: Conservé la campanilla, porque todavía quería encontrar de nuevo al barquero.
ending.english: I kept the little bell, because I still wanted to find the boatman again.

ending.spanish: Cuando volvió el viento, pude elevarme por encima del tejado.
ending.english: When the wind returned, I could rise above the roof.

ending.spanish: Mi cuaderno pesaba menos que una sola piedra.
ending.english: My notebook weighed less than a single stone.

ending.spanish: Sin embargo, llevaba dentro todos los lugares de los que me había costado despedirme.
ending.english: Yet it held all the places I had found it hard to leave.

author: Zumi
title: La biblioteca que voló
summary: Zumi’s flying library cannot lift a single book, so his smallest readers help him rethink the invention.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Mi biblioteca voladora tenía alas, una hélice y un letrero precioso.
sentences.english: My flying library had wings, a propeller and a beautiful sign.

sentences.spanish: Lo único que no podía hacer era volar con libros.
sentences.english: The only thing it could not do was fly with books.

sentences.spanish: Quité el letrero, después el techo y finalmente mi asiento.
sentences.english: I removed the sign, then the roof and finally my seat.

sentences.spanish: La máquina seguía pegada al suelo.
sentences.english: The machine remained stuck to the ground.

sentences.spanish: Un grupo de hormigas esperaba su primer cuento junto a la rueda.
sentences.english: A group of ants waited for their first story beside the wheel.

sentences.spanish: Me preguntaron por qué necesitaba llevar el libro entero.
sentences.english: They asked me why I needed to carry the whole book.

continuation.spanish: Les expliqué que no iba a arrancar las páginas de un libro prestado.
continuation.english: I explained that I was not going to tear pages out of a borrowed book.

continuation.spanish: «Puedes leerlo tú y contárnoslo», respondió la más pequeña.
continuation.english: “You can read it and tell it to us,” the smallest replied.

continuation.spanish: Aquello no se parecía a mi dibujo de una gran biblioteca.
continuation.english: That did not look like my drawing of a grand library.

continuation.spanish: Pero desmonté la hélice y preparé una bolsa con tarjetas.
continuation.english: But I dismantled the propeller and prepared a bag of cards.

continuation.spanish: En cada tarjeta escribí una escena con permiso de su autor.
continuation.english: On each card I wrote a scene with its author’s permission.

continuation.spanish: Esta vez pude despegar sin dejar nada importante en tierra.
continuation.english: This time I could take off without leaving anything important on the ground.

ending.spanish: Visité tres hormigueros y leí la primera historia en voz alta.
ending.english: I visited three anthills and read the first story aloud.

ending.spanish: Los oyentes pidieron personajes diferentes y un final menos triste.
ending.english: The listeners asked for different characters and a less sad ending.

ending.spanish: Anoté sus ideas para llevárselas al autor.
ending.english: I wrote down their ideas to take them to the author.

ending.spanish: Al regresar, mi máquina vacía parecía mucho menos interesante.
ending.english: When I returned, my empty machine looked much less interesting.

ending.spanish: Colgué el letrero en mi bolsa y prometí volver el viernes.
ending.english: I hung the sign on my bag and promised to return on Friday.

ending.spanish: La biblioteca ya volaba, aunque no de la forma que yo había imaginado.
ending.english: The library was flying now, although not in the way I had imagined.

author: Musgo
title: La semilla que buscaba casa
englishTitle: The Seed Looking for a Home
summary: A seed refuses every pot Musgo offers it, leaving muddy footprints towards a house nobody visits.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La semilla salió de la maceta durante la noche.
sentences.english: The seed climbed out of the flowerpot during the night.

sentences.spanish: Por la mañana encontré huellas de barro sobre mi mesa.
sentences.english: In the morning I found muddy footprints on my table.

sentences.spanish: La puse en una maceta más grande, pero volvió a escapar.
sentences.english: I put it in a larger pot, but it escaped again.

sentences.spanish: Intenté hablarle en la lengua antigua de las raíces.
sentences.english: I tried speaking to it in the ancient language of roots.

sentences.spanish: Solo contestó con un pequeño salto hacia la ventana.
sentences.english: It answered only with a little jump towards the window.

sentences.spanish: Decidí seguirla antes de buscar otro hechizo.
sentences.english: I decided to follow it before looking for another spell.

continuation.spanish: Cruzó el jardín, la plaza y el puente de piedra.
continuation.english: It crossed the garden, the square and the stone bridge.

continuation.spanish: Yo caminaba detrás con una regadera y bastante vergüenza.
continuation.english: I walked behind with a watering can and considerable embarrassment.

continuation.spanish: Se detuvo ante una casa que llevaba meses cerrada.
continuation.english: It stopped outside a house that had been closed for months.

continuation.spanish: Una joven abrió la puerta y reconoció la semilla.
continuation.english: A young woman opened the door and recognised the seed.

continuation.spanish: Su abuela me la había dado antes de que ella llegara al pueblo.
continuation.english: Her grandmother had given it to me before she arrived in the village.

continuation.spanish: «Decía que estas flores siempre encuentran a la familia», murmuró.
continuation.english: “She said these flowers always find the family,” she murmured.

ending.spanish: Plantamos la semilla bajo la ventana de la cocina.
ending.english: We planted the seed beneath the kitchen window.

ending.spanish: Esta vez no intentó salir de la tierra.
ending.english: This time it did not try to climb out of the soil.

ending.spanish: La joven me invitó a tomar té mientras limpiaba dos sillas.
ending.english: The young woman invited me for tea while she cleaned two chairs.

ending.spanish: Le conté historias de su abuela que ella no conocía.
ending.english: I told her stories about her grandmother that she did not know.

ending.spanish: Cuando me fui, una hoja asomaba junto a la pared.
ending.english: When I left, a leaf was emerging beside the wall.

ending.spanish: Volví a casa con la maceta vacía y una invitación para el domingo.
ending.english: I returned home with the empty pot and an invitation for Sunday.

author: Zumi
title: El reloj del invernadero
summary: Zumi must discover why the greenhouse has sealed itself shut before its plants wilt in the heat.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: El reloj del invernadero marcó las doce y todas las ventanas se cerraron de golpe.
sentences.english: The greenhouse clock struck twelve and every window slammed shut.

sentences.spanish: Zumi dejó caer su destornillador; fuera todavía estaba amaneciendo.
sentences.english: Zumi dropped his screwdriver; outside, dawn was only just breaking.

sentences.spanish: Dentro, las tomateras se inclinaban por el calor y una abeja golpeaba el cristal.
sentences.english: Inside, the tomato plants were drooping in the heat and a bee was striking the glass.

sentences.spanish: Alguien había adelantado el reloj, pero la puerta estaba cerrada desde la noche anterior.
sentences.english: Someone had put the clock forward, but the door had been locked since the night before.

continuation.spanish: Zumi entró por un tubo de riego, con una cuerda atada a la cintura.
continuation.english: Zumi entered through an irrigation pipe, with a rope tied around his waist.

continuation.spanish: En la maquinaria encontró hilos de seda y una diminuta hamaca.
continuation.english: In the mechanism he found silk threads and a tiny hammock.

continuation.spanish: Una araña había movido una rueda para que su cama quedara a la sombra.
continuation.english: A spider had moved a gear to keep her bed in the shade.

continuation.spanish: —Solo quería dormir —dijo ella, mirando las hojas caídas.
continuation.english: “I only wanted to sleep,” she said, looking at the drooping leaves.

ending.spanish: La pequeña mosca detuvo el mecanismo con su destornillador y Faro abrió las ventanas desde fuera.
ending.english: The little fly stopped the mechanism with his screwdriver, and Faro opened the windows from outside.

ending.spanish: Después construyeron una hamaca bajo una maceta, lejos de las ruedas.
ending.english: Afterwards they built a hammock beneath a flowerpot, away from the gears.

ending.spanish: Zumi añadió una manivela para abrir las ventanas si el reloj volvía a fallar.
ending.english: Zumi added a crank to open the windows if the clock failed again.

ending.spanish: A mediodía, la abeja salió libre y la araña, por fin, durmió hasta las doce de verdad.
ending.english: At midday, the bee flew free and the spider finally slept until the real twelve o’clock.

author: Luma
title: El jardín que perdió el azul
englishTitle: The Garden That Lost Its Blue
summary: A moth follows a stolen colour into an unfinished painting.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Luma conocía cada flor del jardín, por eso notó enseguida que faltaba el azul.
sentences.english: Luma knew every flower in the garden, so she immediately noticed that the blue was missing.

sentences.spanish: Las campanillas eran grises y el estanque reflejaba un cielo sin color.
sentences.english: The bluebells were grey, and the pond reflected a colourless sky.
