sentences.spanish: Sobre el muro había una mancha azul que temblaba, aunque no soplaba viento.
sentences.english: On the wall was a blue stain that trembled, although no wind was blowing.

sentences.spanish: La polilla la tocó con una antena y cayó dentro de un cuadro.
sentences.english: The moth touched it with an antenna and fell into a painting.

continuation.spanish: Al otro lado, un pintor diminuto intentaba terminar un mar para su hija.
continuation.english: On the other side, a tiny painter was trying to finish a sea for his daughter.

continuation.spanish: —Nunca lo ha visto —explicó—. Pensé que no echaríais de menos un poco de azul.
continuation.english: “She has never seen it,” he explained. “I thought you wouldn’t miss a little blue.”

continuation.spanish: Pero cada ola que pintaba bebía más color del jardín, y el mar crecía sin detenerse.
continuation.english: But every wave he painted drank more colour from the garden, and the sea kept growing.

continuation.spanish: Luma voló hasta el borde del lienzo; el agua ya alcanzaba la firma del pintor.
continuation.english: Luma flew to the edge of the canvas; the water had already reached the painter’s signature.

ending.spanish: —Un mar también necesita una orilla —gritó, y arrastró el pincel hacia la tierra seca.
ending.english: “A sea needs a shore too,” she shouted, dragging the brush towards dry land.

ending.spanish: Entre los dos pintaron una playa que contuvo las olas y una puerta para devolver los colores.
ending.english: Together they painted a beach that held back the waves and a door to return the colours.

ending.spanish: La hija llegó al atardecer y se sentó ante el cuadro, sin pedir que fuera más grande.
ending.english: His daughter arrived at dusk and sat before the painting, without asking for it to be bigger.

ending.spanish: Luma volvió al jardín con una sola mota azul en el ala: el pintor se la había regalado.
ending.english: Luma returned to the garden with a single blue speck on her wing: the painter had given it to her.

author: Faro
title: La cesta bajo el puente
summary: Faro and Benji follow muddy footprints to a secret midnight meal.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Faro esperaba a Benji junto al granero, pero su amigo ratón no apareció.
sentences.english: Faro was waiting for Benji beside the barn, but his mouse friend did not appear.

sentences.spanish: En su lugar llegó una cesta de patatas que bajaba sola por el camino.
sentences.english: Instead, a basket of potatoes came down the path on its own.

sentences.spanish: El búho abrió las alas y aterrizó delante de ella.
sentences.english: The owl spread his wings and landed in front of it.

sentences.spanish: —No mires dentro —dijo una voz conocida desde debajo de la cesta.
sentences.english: “Don’t look inside,” said a familiar voice from beneath the basket.

continuation.spanish: Benji estaba empujando la comida hacia el puente y tenía las patas llenas de barro.
continuation.english: Benji was pushing the food towards the bridge, and his paws were covered in mud.

continuation.spanish: Le pidió a Faro que vigilara el camino, como tantas otras noches.
continuation.english: He asked Faro to watch the path, as he had on so many other nights.

continuation.spanish: Esta vez, sin embargo, el búho oyó un llanto pequeño entre las piedras.
continuation.english: This time, however, the owl heard a little sob among the stones.

continuation.spanish: Bajo el puente, una familia de ratones esperaba a que bajara el río para volver a casa.
continuation.english: Beneath the bridge, a family of mice was waiting for the river to fall so they could go home.

ending.spanish: Faro llevó las patatas de una en una hasta una repisa seca del granero.
ending.english: Faro carried the potatoes one by one to a dry shelf in the barn.

ending.spanish: Benji guio a la familia por un túnel que el búho era demasiado grande para cruzar.
ending.english: Benji guided the family through a tunnel that the owl was too large to enter.

ending.spanish: Al amanecer compartieron una cena tardía a la luz de una vela.
ending.english: At dawn they shared a late dinner by candlelight.

ending.spanish: Faro escribió hasta quedarse dormido, y Benji le puso una patata caliente junto a la taza.
ending.english: Faro wrote until he fell asleep, and Benji put a hot potato beside his cup.

author: Mora
title: Dos zanahorias y un dragón
summary: Mora’s shopping trip becomes an unexpected lesson in feeding a very small dragon.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Mora lleva dos zanahorias al mercado: una para ella y otra para Pipa.
sentences.english: Mora is taking two carrots to the market: one for herself and one for Pipa.

sentences.spanish: En el camino ve humo detrás de una piedra.
sentences.english: On the path she sees smoke behind a stone.

sentences.spanish: —¿Brasa? —pregunta la duendecilla, pero la piedra estornuda.
sentences.english: “Brasa?” asks the sprite, but the stone sneezes.

sentences.spanish: Es un dragón muy pequeño, con una olla en la cabeza.
sentences.english: It is a very small dragon, with a pot on his head.

continuation.spanish: El dragón no puede ver el camino y tiene mucha hambre.
continuation.english: The dragon cannot see the path and is very hungry.

continuation.spanish: Mora tira de la olla, pero no sale.
continuation.english: Mora pulls the pot, but it does not come off.

continuation.spanish: El pequeño huele las zanahorias y abre mucho la boca.
continuation.english: The little one smells the carrots and opens his mouth wide.

continuation.spanish: Entonces estornuda otra vez: la olla sale volando y cae en un árbol.
continuation.english: Then he sneezes again: the pot flies off and lands in a tree.

ending.spanish: Mora le da una zanahoria y guarda la otra.
ending.english: Mora gives him one carrot and keeps the other.

ending.spanish: Pipa llega, mira el árbol y empieza a reír.
ending.english: Pipa arrives, looks at the tree and begins to laugh.

ending.spanish: Los tres comparten la última zanahoria junto al río.
ending.english: The three of them share the last carrot beside the river.

ending.spanish: Ahora el dragón tiene amigos, pero Mora necesita una escalera.
ending.english: Now the dragon has friends, but Mora needs a ladder.

author: Zumi
title: La carrera sin alas
summary: Zumi’s fastest invention takes him further than his tired legs can carry him home.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Zumi quería ganar una carrera a pie con unas botas de muelles; aquel día no valía volar.
sentences.english: Zumi wanted to win a footrace with a pair of spring boots; flying was not allowed that day.

sentences.spanish: Al probarlas saltó por encima de Pipa y perdió el desayuno que llevaba en la mano.
sentences.english: When he tried them, he jumped over Pipa and lost the breakfast he was holding.

sentences.spanish: —¡Funcionan! —gritó, mientras su pan con miel caía al suelo.
sentences.english: “They work!” he shouted, as his bread and honey fell to the ground.

sentences.spanish: No paró a comer ni a descansar antes de la salida.
sentences.english: He did not stop to eat or rest before the start.

continuation.spanish: Durante la carrera dejó atrás a todos, hasta que sus piernas empezaron a temblar.
continuation.english: During the race he left everyone behind, until his legs began to shake.

continuation.spanish: Las botas lo llevaron al otro lado de un arroyo; cayó en el barro y se mojó las alas.
continuation.english: The boots took him across a stream; he fell in the mud and got his wings wet.

continuation.spanish: Oyó que los demás corredores pasaban por el puente y quiso llamarlos.
continuation.english: He heard the other runners crossing the bridge and wanted to call them.

continuation.spanish: Le daba vergüenza, aunque estaba solo y empezaba a tener frío.
continuation.english: He was embarrassed, although he was alone and starting to feel cold.

ending.spanish: Por fin gritó, y Pipa volvió con agua, comida y una manta.
ending.english: At last he shouted, and Pipa returned with water, food and a blanket.

ending.spanish: Descansaron juntos hasta que Zumi pudo caminar despacio.
ending.english: They rested together until Zumi could walk slowly.

ending.spanish: Al llegar a la meta, la pequeña mosca pidió ayuda para quitarse las botas.
ending.english: When they reached the finish, the little fly asked for help taking off his boots.

ending.spanish: Al día siguiente añadió un freno a su invento y una pausa para desayunar a su plan.
ending.english: The next day he added a brake to his invention and a breakfast break to his plan.

author: Brasa
title: El brindis del farero
summary: Brasa arrives at a farewell party just as the lighthouse goes dark.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Brasa llegó al faro con una tarta que había calentado demasiado.
sentences.english: Brasa arrived at the lighthouse with a cake he had heated too much.

sentences.spanish: El farero se jubilaba aquella noche y había invitado a todos sus vecinos.
sentences.english: The lighthouse keeper was retiring that night and had invited all his neighbours.

sentences.spanish: Cuando levantaron los vasos para brindar, la luz del faro se apagó.
sentences.english: When they raised their glasses for a toast, the lighthouse went out.

sentences.spanish: Desde el mar llegó el sonido de un barco que se acercaba a las rocas.
sentences.english: From the sea came the sound of a boat approaching the rocks.

continuation.spanish: El dragón subió la escalera y encendió una llama frente al gran espejo.
continuation.english: The dragon climbed the stairs and lit a flame in front of the great mirror.

continuation.spanish: La luz volvió al mar, pero Brasa no podía mantener el fuego mucho tiempo.
continuation.english: Light returned to the sea, but Brasa could not keep the fire going for long.

continuation.spanish: Abajo, los vecinos formaron una fila para pasar las herramientas del farero.
continuation.english: Below, the neighbours formed a line to pass up the keeper’s tools.

continuation.spanish: Él reparó la lámpara mientras su futura sustituta hacía girar el espejo a mano.
continuation.english: He repaired the lamp while his future replacement turned the mirror by hand.

ending.spanish: El barco respondió con tres luces y se alejó de las rocas.
ending.english: The boat answered with three lights and moved away from the rocks.

ending.spanish: Cuando bajaron, nadie pidió un discurso: todos necesitaban sentarse.
ending.english: When they came down, nobody asked for a speech: everyone needed to sit down.

ending.spanish: Brasa levantó un vaso de agua fría con las dos manos.
ending.english: Brasa raised a glass of cold water with both hands.

ending.spanish: La tarta estaba quemada por fuera, pero aquella noche no quedó ni una miga.
ending.english: The cake was burnt on the outside, but that night not a crumb remained.

author: Luma
title: El puente de las preguntas
summary: A curious fox finds that knowing the right question matters more than having a quick answer.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Foxy llevaba una libreta llena de cosas que todavía no sabía hacer.
sentences.english: Foxy carried a notebook full of things he did not yet know how to do.

sentences.spanish: Aquella mañana añadió «cruzar el puente del barranco», aunque el puente había desaparecido.
sentences.english: That morning he added “cross the ravine bridge,” although the bridge had disappeared.

sentences.spanish: En su lugar flotaban tres piedras y un cartel que decía: «Pregunta antes de saltar».
sentences.english: In its place floated three stones and a sign saying, “Ask before you jump.”

sentences.spanish: El zorro preguntó cuánto debía saltar, y la primera piedra se alejó.
sentences.english: The fox asked how far he should jump, and the first stone moved away.

continuation.spanish: Probó preguntas sobre la velocidad, el viento y el peso de su mochila.
continuation.english: He tried questions about speed, wind and the weight of his backpack.

continuation.spanish: Cada vez, las piedras se separaban un poco más.
continuation.english: Each time, the stones moved a little further apart.

continuation.spanish: Entonces oyó a alguien llorar debajo del cartel: era la guardiana del puente.
continuation.english: Then he heard someone crying beneath the sign: it was the bridge keeper.

continuation.spanish: Foxy cerró la libreta y le preguntó por qué estaba triste.
continuation.english: Foxy closed his notebook and asked her why she was sad.

ending.spanish: La guardiana explicó que todos le pedían caminos, pero nadie se quedaba a conversar.
ending.english: The keeper explained that everyone asked her for routes, but nobody stayed to talk.

ending.spanish: Mientras compartían sus recuerdos, las piedras volvieron a reunirse sobre el barranco.
ending.english: As they shared their memories, the stones came together again above the ravine.

ending.spanish: El zorro cruzó al atardecer, después de prometer que regresaría con una historia.
ending.english: The fox crossed at dusk, after promising to return with a story.

ending.spanish: En la libreta tachó su primera nota y escribió: «Volver el jueves. Llevar dos tazas».
ending.english: In his notebook he crossed out his first note and wrote, “Return on Thursday. Bring two cups.”

author: Faro
title: La página que falta
summary: Foxy borrows an adventure with no ending and sets out to find its missing page.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Foxy lee un libro bajo un árbol.
sentences.english: Foxy reads a book beneath a tree.

sentences.spanish: Un viajero busca una llave, pero la última página no está.
sentences.english: A traveller is looking for a key, but the last page is missing.

sentences.spanish: —Necesito saber dónde está la llave —dice el zorro.
sentences.english: “I need to know where the key is,” says the fox.

sentences.spanish: Dentro del libro hay una pluma blanca y una dirección.
sentences.english: Inside the book there is a white feather and an address.

continuation.spanish: Foxy sigue la dirección hasta una casa pequeña junto al molino.
continuation.english: Foxy follows the address to a small house beside the mill.

continuation.spanish: Una anciana abre la puerta y reconoce su libro.
continuation.english: An old woman opens the door and recognises her book.

continuation.spanish: —La última página está en mi bolsillo —dice—. No me gusta el final.
continuation.english: “The last page is in my pocket,” she says. “I don’t like the ending.”

continuation.spanish: En ese final, el viajero encuentra la llave, pero vuelve solo a casa.
continuation.english: In that ending, the traveller finds the key but returns home alone.

ending.spanish: Foxy se sienta con ella y propone otro final.
ending.english: Foxy sits with her and suggests another ending.

ending.spanish: El viajero abre una puerta y encuentra a un amigo al otro lado.
ending.english: The traveller opens a door and finds a friend on the other side.

ending.spanish: La anciana escribe la nueva página y pone el libro sobre la mesa.
ending.english: The old woman writes the new page and puts the book on the table.

ending.spanish: Antes de irse, Foxy pregunta si puede volver para leer el siguiente.
ending.english: Before leaving, Foxy asks if he can return to read the next one.

author: Faro
title: El monstruo de las campanas
summary: Faro follows a terrifying farm legend into the one place his neighbours refuse to enter.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: En la granja decían que, cuando sonaban campanas en el bosque, alguien perdía su sombra.
sentences.english: On the farm they said that, when bells rang in the forest, someone lost their shadow.

sentences.spanish: Faro había escrito aquella leyenda muchas veces sin abandonar la seguridad del granero.
sentences.english: Faro had written that legend many times without leaving the safety of the barn.

sentences.spanish: Una noche sonaron tres campanadas y Benji no volvió de su ronda.
sentences.english: One night three bells rang, and Benji did not return from his rounds.

sentences.spanish: El búho tomó una vela, aunque sus ojos veían mejor sin ella.
sentences.english: The owl took a candle, although his eyes saw better without it.

continuation.spanish: Encontró la bufanda del ratón junto a un pozo y oyó su voz desde el fondo.
continuation.english: He found the mouse’s scarf beside a well and heard his voice from the bottom.

continuation.spanish: Una criatura enorme inclinó la cabeza sobre ellos, con campanas colgadas de los cuernos.
continuation.english: An enormous creature bent its head over them, with bells hanging from its horns.

continuation.spanish: Faro quiso huir, hasta que vio que la criatura sujetaba una cuerda entre los dientes.
continuation.english: Faro wanted to flee, until he saw that the creature was holding a rope between its teeth.

continuation.spanish: Llevaba horas intentando sacar a Benji, pero sus pezuñas no podían hacer un nudo.
continuation.english: It had been trying for hours to pull Benji out, but its hooves could not tie a knot.

ending.spanish: Faro ató la cuerda a una rama y bajó el extremo hasta su amigo.
ending.english: Faro tied the rope to a branch and lowered the end to his friend.

ending.spanish: Cuando Benji estuvo a salvo, la criatura pidió que no contaran dónde vivía.
ending.english: Once Benji was safe, the creature asked them not to tell anyone where it lived.

ending.spanish: El búho cambió su leyenda: conservó las campanas, pero dejó fuera el camino hasta el pozo.
ending.english: The owl changed his legend: he kept the bells but left out the path to the well.

ending.spanish: Desde entonces, en las noches frías, alguien deja una manta grande en el límite del bosque.
ending.english: Since then, on cold nights, someone leaves a large blanket at the edge of the forest.

author: Pipa
title: La mochila de las despedidas
summary: Pipa misses his bus because one goodbye is more difficult than all the others.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Pipa podía hacer la mochila en cinco minutos, pero nunca sabía despedirse.
sentences.english: Pipa could pack his backpack in five minutes, but he never knew how to say goodbye.

sentences.spanish: En cada ciudad dejaba una nota y salía antes de que sus amigos despertaran.
sentences.english: In every city he left a note and departed before his friends woke up.

sentences.spanish: Aquella mañana, en un pueblo junto al mar, encontró a su anfitriona sentada sobre la mochila.
sentences.english: That morning, in a seaside village, he found his host sitting on his backpack.

sentences.spanish: —Esta vez vas a desayunar conmigo —dijo ella.
sentences.english: “This time you’re having breakfast with me,” she said.

continuation.spanish: El autobús salía pronto y Pipa miraba la puerta entre cada bocado.
continuation.english: The bus was leaving soon, and Pipa looked at the door between each bite.

continuation.spanish: Su amiga le preguntó por el mejor momento de la visita, y el lagarto dejó de mirar el reloj.
continuation.english: His friend asked about the best moment of his visit, and the lizard stopped looking at the clock.

continuation.spanish: Recordaron una noche sin luz y una canción que ninguno sabía cantar.
continuation.english: They remembered a night without electricity and a song that neither of them knew how to sing.

continuation.spanish: Cuando llegaron a la estación, el autobús ya doblaba la esquina.
continuation.english: When they reached the station, the bus was already turning the corner.

ending.spanish: Pipa buscó otra salida y compró un billete para la tarde.
ending.english: Pipa looked for another departure and bought a ticket for the afternoon.

ending.spanish: Tuvieron tiempo de caminar hasta el puerto y de decir lo que la nota no decía.
ending.english: They had time to walk to the harbour and say what the note did not say.

ending.spanish: Esta vez, al subir al autobús, Pipa no fingió que tenía polvo en los ojos.
ending.english: This time, when he got on the bus, Pipa did not pretend he had dust in his eyes.

ending.spanish: Desde la ventana vio a su amiga despedirse hasta que el camino los separó.
ending.english: From the window he watched his friend waving until the road separated them.

author: Pipa
title: La etiqueta escondida
summary: A celebrated designer offers Pipa success on one uncomfortable condition.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: El abrigo de Pipa apareció en el escaparate más famoso de la ciudad, pero llevaba otro nombre.
sentences.english: Pipa’s coat appeared in the city’s most famous shop window, but it bore someone else’s name.

sentences.spanish: El dueño le explicó que una firma conocida vendía más que la de un lagarto viajero.
sentences.english: The owner explained that a famous signature sold better than that of a travelling lizard.

sentences.spanish: Pipa necesitaba el dinero para continuar su viaje y estuvo a punto de aceptar.
sentences.english: Pipa needed the money to continue his journey and almost accepted.

sentences.spanish: Entonces vio que también habían quitado el bolsillo secreto que había diseñado para guardar cartas.
sentences.english: Then he saw that they had also removed the secret pocket he had designed for keeping letters.

continuation.spanish: Volvió al taller donde había cosido el abrigo durante varias noches de lluvia.
continuation.english: He returned to the workshop where he had sewn the coat over several rainy nights.

continuation.spanish: La costurera que le había prestado la máquina le preguntó qué quería conservar de su trabajo.
continuation.english: The seamstress who had lent him the machine asked what he wanted to preserve in his work.

continuation.spanish: Pipa pensó en las despedidas, en las cartas arrugadas y en las personas que no cabían en una maleta.
continuation.english: Pipa thought of goodbyes, crumpled letters and people who could not fit inside a suitcase.

continuation.spanish: Al día siguiente llevó al escaparate una etiqueta nueva y su pequeño bolsillo.
continuation.english: The next day he took a new label and his little pocket to the shop window.

ending.spanish: El dueño rechazó los cambios, así que Pipa retiró el abrigo y perdió aquel encargo.
ending.english: The owner rejected the changes, so Pipa took back the coat and lost that commission.

ending.spanish: La costurera le ofreció un rincón del taller para mostrarlo durante una semana.
ending.english: The seamstress offered him a corner of her workshop to display it for a week.

ending.spanish: Solo llegó una clienta, que metió la mano en el bolsillo y sonrió al encontrar espacio para una carta.
ending.english: Only one customer came; she slipped her hand into the pocket and smiled when she found room for a letter.

ending.spanish: Pipa tuvo que retrasar su viaje, pero aquella venta llevaba su nombre por dentro y por fuera.
ending.english: Pipa had to postpone his trip, but that sale carried his name inside and out.

author: Pipa
title: La casa que cambió de puerta
englishTitle: The House with a Different Door
summary: After years travelling, Pipa returns home and discovers that coming back is another kind of adventure.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Después de cuatro años de viaje, Pipa volvió a su calle y no encontró su puerta roja.
sentences.english: After four years travelling, Pipa returned to his street and could not find his red door.

sentences.spanish: En su lugar había una puerta azul y una bicicleta que no conocía.
sentences.english: In its place was a blue door and a bicycle he did not recognise.

sentences.spanish: Llamó dos veces, preparado para explicar que se había equivocado.
sentences.english: He knocked twice, ready to explain that he had made a mistake.

sentences.spanish: Su hermana abrió y le dijo que llevaba toda la mañana esperando.
sentences.english: His sister opened it and said she had been waiting all morning.

continuation.spanish: Dentro, su antiguo despacho era ahora un taller lleno de telas y plantas.
continuation.english: Inside, his old office was now a workshop full of fabrics and plants.

continuation.spanish: Pipa quiso contar sus aventuras, pero primero preguntó qué había pasado allí durante su ausencia.
continuation.english: Pipa wanted to tell his adventures, but first he asked what had happened there while he was away.

continuation.spanish: Su hermana le enseñó una máquina nueva y una silla vacía junto a la ventana.
continuation.english: His sister showed him a new machine and an empty chair beside the window.

continuation.spanish: —No guardé tu cuarto —dijo—, pero sí un sitio para trabajar contigo.
continuation.english: “I didn’t keep your room,” she said, “but I did keep a place to work with you.”

ending.spanish: Pasaron la tarde arreglando una chaqueta mientras Pipa aprendía a usar la máquina.
ending.english: They spent the afternoon mending a jacket while Pipa learned to use the machine.

ending.spanish: Él habló de los caminos y ella de los días en que el taller casi tuvo que cerrar.
ending.english: He talked about the roads, and she about the days when the workshop had nearly had to close.

ending.spanish: Al anochecer Pipa colgó su mochila junto a la puerta azul.
ending.english: At nightfall Pipa hung his backpack beside the blue door.

ending.spanish: Todavía no sabía cuánto tiempo iba a quedarse, pero ya sabía qué harían al día siguiente.
ending.english: He still did not know how long he would stay, but he already knew what they would do the next day.

author: Nube
title: El martes que no llegaba
summary: Nube keeps postponing a visit until a strange calendar starts erasing the days.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Nube tenía una invitación para tomar té con una amiga en la montaña.
sentences.english: Nube had an invitation to have tea with a friend in the mountains.

sentences.spanish: Cada semana escribía «el próximo martes» y buscaba una excusa para quedarse.
sentences.english: Every week he wrote “next Tuesday” and found an excuse to stay.

sentences.spanish: Una mañana descubrió que todos los martes habían desaparecido de su calendario.
sentences.english: One morning he discovered that all the Tuesdays had disappeared from his calendar.

sentences.spanish: Bajo la última página había una nota de Musgo: «Este calendario cree lo que dices».
sentences.english: Beneath the last page was a note from Musgo: “This calendar believes what you say.”

continuation.spanish: Nube fue a buscar al mago, pero solo encontró una caja de días usados.
continuation.english: Nube went to find the wizard but found only a box of used days.

continuation.spanish: Dentro estaban los martes perdidos, doblados como pequeñas cartas.
continuation.english: Inside were the lost Tuesdays, folded like little letters.

continuation.spanish: En cada uno aparecía su amiga poniendo dos tazas y guardando una después.
continuation.english: In each one he saw his friend setting out two cups and putting one away afterwards.

continuation.spanish: Nube comprendió por qué le costaba subir: temía que ya no tuvieran nada que contarse.
continuation.english: Nube understood why he found it hard to go up: he feared they would no longer have anything to tell each other.

ending.spanish: Dejó la caja cerrada y salió hacia la montaña aquella misma tarde.
ending.english: He left the box closed and set off for the mountains that very afternoon.

ending.spanish: Su amiga abrió la puerta y dijo que el té se había acabado, pero quedaba sopa.
ending.english: His friend opened the door and said the tea was gone, but there was soup left.

ending.spanish: Hablaron hasta que las ventanas se cubrieron de vaho.
ending.english: They talked until the windows steamed up.

ending.spanish: Al regresar, Nube encontró un martes nuevo en el calendario y escribió una fecha concreta para volver.
ending.english: When he returned, Nube found a new Tuesday in the calendar and wrote down a specific date to go back.

matchGlossary.contarse: to be told / to tell one another

author: Faro
title: La vaca del otro lado
englishTitle: The Cow on the Other Side
summary: Two farms claim the same missing cow, and Faro must listen beyond their argument.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La vaca apareció entre las dos granjas con una cinta roja y una campana azul.
sentences.english: The cow appeared between the two farms with a red ribbon and a blue bell.

sentences.spanish: Una familia la llamaba Estrella; la otra insistía en que se llamaba Luna.
sentences.english: One family called her Estrella; the other insisted her name was Luna.

sentences.spanish: Faro, que quería dormir después de escribir toda la noche, recibió el encargo de resolver la disputa.
sentences.english: Faro, who wanted to sleep after writing all night, was asked to settle the dispute.

sentences.spanish: Mientras todos gritaban su nombre favorito, la vaca miraba hacia el bosque.
sentences.english: While everyone shouted their preferred name, the cow looked towards the forest.

continuation.spanish: El búho revisó dibujos, recibos y recuerdos que demostraban historias diferentes.
continuation.english: The owl examined drawings, receipts and memories that supported different stories.

continuation.spanish: Benji, cansado de escuchar, abrió la verja y siguió a la vaca a una distancia prudente.
continuation.english: Benji, tired of listening, opened the gate and followed the cow at a careful distance.

continuation.spanish: Ella caminó hasta una zanja donde un ternero no conseguía subir por el barro.
continuation.english: She walked to a ditch where a calf could not climb out through the mud.

continuation.spanish: Faro llamó a las dos familias, que por primera vez dejaron de discutir.
continuation.english: Faro called both families, who stopped arguing for the first time.

ending.spanish: Con una tabla y varias cuerdas sacaron al ternero antes de que empezara a llover.
ending.english: With a plank and several ropes, they got the calf out before it began to rain.

ending.spanish: Después descubrieron que la vaca había pasado el invierno en una granja y el verano en la otra.
ending.english: Afterwards they discovered that the cow had spent winter on one farm and summer on the other.

ending.spanish: Acordaron cuidar de ella juntos mientras buscaban sus antiguos documentos.
ending.english: They agreed to look after her together while they searched for her old records.

ending.spanish: Faro cerró su cuaderno: el asunto del nombre podía esperar hasta después de la siesta.
ending.english: Faro closed his notebook: the question of the name could wait until after his nap.

author: Musgo
title: La caja de la noche
summary: Musgo steals a piece of darkness to finish a spell and finds something alive inside it.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Musgo compró una caja que solo podía abrirse cuando nadie pronunciaba su nombre.
sentences.english: Musgo bought a box that could only be opened when nobody spoke his name.

sentences.spanish: Quería usar la oscuridad de su interior para leer un libro escrito con tinta de estrellas.
sentences.english: He wanted to use the darkness inside it to read a book written in star ink.

sentences.spanish: Esperó hasta medianoche y levantó la tapa en el sótano.
sentences.english: He waited until midnight and lifted the lid in the cellar.

sentences.spanish: Algo golpeó desde dentro tres veces, como un visitante educado que hubiera olvidado dónde estaba la puerta.
sentences.english: Something knocked three times from inside, like a polite visitor who had forgotten where the door was.

continuation.spanish: Del hueco salió una sombra que adoptó la forma de Musgo cuando era joven.
continuation.english: A shadow emerged from the hollow and took the shape of Musgo when he was young.

continuation.spanish: Le ofreció terminar todos los hechizos que había abandonado, si le entregaba su nombre.
continuation.english: It offered to finish every spell he had abandoned if he gave it his name.

continuation.spanish: El mago empezó a responder, pero vio que las letras de sus libros se borraban a su alrededor.
continuation.english: The wizard began to answer, but saw the letters in his books fading around him.

continuation.spanish: Cada promesa de la sombra necesitaba una historia que devorar.
continuation.english: Every promise the shadow made needed a story to devour.

ending.spanish: Musgo cerró el libro de estrellas y llamó a Faro por la ventana del sótano.
ending.english: Musgo closed the star book and called to Faro through the cellar window.

ending.spanish: El búho gritó el nombre del mago, y la sombra retrocedió hasta la caja.
ending.english: The owl shouted the wizard’s name, and the shadow retreated into the box.

ending.spanish: La tapa cayó antes de que pudiera ofrecerles una última maravilla.
ending.english: The lid fell shut before it could offer them one last wonder.

ending.spanish: Musgo selló la caja y escribió su nombre por fuera; algunos libros podían seguir sin leerse.
ending.english: Musgo sealed the box and wrote his name on the outside; some books could remain unread.

author: Luma
title: La escalera de niebla
summary: Luma chases a light above the clouds and must find a way back before sunrise.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Desde su ventana, Luma vio una lámpara suspendida por encima de la niebla.
sentences.english: From her window, Luma saw a lamp suspended above the mist.

sentences.spanish: Cada noche estaba más cerca, como si alguien la invitara a subir.
sentences.english: Each night it was closer, as though someone were inviting her up.

sentences.spanish: La polilla siguió una escalera de luz hasta una torre sin suelo.
sentences.english: The moth followed a staircase of light to a tower with no floor.

sentences.spanish: Dentro había cientos de lámparas y una cuidadora que no recordaba el camino de vuelta.
sentences.english: Inside were hundreds of lamps and a keeper who could not remember the way back.

continuation.spanish: La cuidadora había reunido luces tan hermosas que había dejado de mirar hacia abajo.
continuation.english: The keeper had gathered lights so beautiful that she had stopped looking down.

continuation.spanish: Ahora la niebla ocultaba incluso el primer peldaño, y el amanecer disolvería la escalera.
continuation.english: Now the mist hid even the first step, and dawn would dissolve the staircase.

continuation.spanish: Luma intentó volar hacia el suelo, pero cada reflejo la devolvía a la misma ventana.
continuation.english: Luma tried to fly towards the ground, but every reflection brought her back to the same window.

continuation.spanish: Entonces reconoció, muy lejos, el olor de la tierra mojada del jardín.
continuation.english: Then, far away, she recognised the smell of the garden’s wet earth.

ending.spanish: Pidió que apagaran las lámparas una a una, aunque a la cuidadora le dolía dejarlas.
ending.english: She asked for the lamps to be extinguished one by one, although the keeper found it painful to leave them.

ending.spanish: Sin tantos reflejos pudieron distinguir una luz pequeña y fija: la ventana de casa de Luma.
ending.english: Without so many reflections, they could make out one small, steady light: the window of Luma’s home.

ending.spanish: Bajaron juntas mientras el último peldaño desaparecía detrás de ellas.
ending.english: They descended together as the last step disappeared behind them.

ending.spanish: La cuidadora conservó una sola lámpara, y aquella mañana la colgó junto a una puerta de verdad.
ending.english: The keeper kept just one lamp, and that morning she hung it beside a real door.

author: Nube
title: La sombra del mediodía
summary: Nube follows a moving shadow across a market and accidentally becomes part of a street performance.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Nube llegó a una ciudad calurosa y se detuvo sobre una plaza llena de músicos.
sentences.english: Nube arrived in a hot city and stopped above a square full of musicians.

sentences.spanish: Abajo, un niño corría detrás de su sombra con una silla.
sentences.english: Below, a child was running after his shadow with a chair.

sentences.spanish: Cada vez que Nube avanzaba, el niño cambiaba la silla de sitio.
sentences.english: Every time Nube moved forward, the child moved the chair.

sentences.spanish: La nube bajó un poco para preguntar por qué lo seguía.
sentences.english: The cloud lowered himself a little to ask why the child was following him.

continuation.spanish: El niño quería que su abuela pudiera ver el concierto sin sentarse al sol.
continuation.english: The child wanted his grandmother to watch the concert without sitting in the sun.

continuation.spanish: Nube prometió quedarse quieto, pero un viento fuerte empezó a empujarlo.
continuation.english: Nube promised to stay still, but a strong wind began pushing him.

continuation.spanish: La abuela abrió su paraguas y el niño movió la silla al ritmo de la música.
continuation.english: The grandmother opened her umbrella, and the child moved the chair to the rhythm of the music.

continuation.spanish: Pronto varios vecinos los siguieron, riendo, con sus propias sillas.
continuation.english: Soon several neighbours followed them, laughing, with their own chairs.

ending.spanish: Los músicos caminaron con ellos hasta una calle estrecha donde había sombra.
ending.english: The musicians walked with them to a narrow street where there was shade.

ending.spanish: Allí terminaron el concierto, y la abuela pidió una canción más.
ending.english: There they finished the concert, and the grandmother asked for one more song.

ending.spanish: Nube tuvo que seguir su viaje, pero oyó el aplauso desde muy lejos.
ending.english: Nube had to continue his journey, but he heard the applause from far away.

ending.spanish: En su cuaderno dibujó una plaza vacía y una calle llena de sillas.
ending.english: In his notebook he drew an empty square and a street full of chairs.

author: Nube
title: El puerto sin tierra
summary: Nube reaches a floating harbour whose residents are waiting for a captain who may never return.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Nube encontró el puerto donde terminaban todos sus mapas, pero no había tierra bajo los barcos.
sentences.english: Nube found the harbour where all his maps ended, but there was no land beneath the boats.

sentences.spanish: Las casas flotaban sujetas a un faro y los vecinos hablaban de un capitán que iba a remolcarlas hasta la costa.
sentences.english: The houses floated tethered to a lighthouse, and the neighbours spoke of a captain who would tow them to shore.

sentences.spanish: Llevaban tanto tiempo esperando que algunos niños nunca habían visto un árbol.
sentences.english: They had been waiting so long that some children had never seen a tree.

sentences.spanish: En la oficina del puerto, Nube encontró una carta que nadie se había atrevido a abrir.
sentences.english: In the harbour office, Nube found a letter that nobody had dared to open.

continuation.spanish: La carta decía que el barco del capitán había naufragado, aunque toda su tripulación estaba a salvo.
continuation.english: The letter said that the captain’s ship had sunk, although all his crew were safe.

continuation.spanish: El capitán pedía ayuda; no prometía regresar a rescatarlos.
continuation.english: The captain was asking for help; he was not promising to return and rescue them.

continuation.spanish: Al escucharla, los vecinos discutieron hasta que una niña señaló las velas guardadas en el almacén.
continuation.english: When they heard it, the neighbours argued until a girl pointed to the sails stored in the warehouse.

continuation.spanish: Si sus casas flotaban, quizá podían aprender a llevarlas ellos mismos.
continuation.english: If their houses floated, perhaps they could learn to steer them themselves.

ending.spanish: Durante varios días repararon velas y ensayaron con una casa vacía.
ending.english: For several days they repaired sails and practised with an empty house.

ending.spanish: Nube subió para vigilar el tiempo y guio la primera salida hacia una bahía protegida.
ending.english: Nube rose to watch the weather and guided the first departure towards a sheltered bay.

ending.spanish: Allí encontraron al capitán, que ya construía un muelle para recibirlos.
ending.english: There they found the captain, who was already building a jetty to receive them.

ending.spanish: Cuando Nube se marchó, el puerto seguía flotando, pero sus habitantes ya sabían elegir el rumbo.
ending.english: When Nube left, the harbour was still floating, but its inhabitants now knew how to choose their course.

author: Tilo
title: La maleta que canta
summary: A station mix-up leaves Pipa holding a suitcase that refuses to stay quiet.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Interior de una estación. Pipa espera con una maleta azul. Algo canta dentro.
sentences.english: Inside a station. Pipa waits with a blue suitcase. Something is singing inside.
sentences.speaker: Narrador

sentences.spanish: Mi ropa no canta. Creo que esta maleta no es mía.
sentences.english: My clothes don’t sing. I think this suitcase isn’t mine.
sentences.speaker: Pipa

sentences.spanish: La mía es azul y lleva una cinta roja. ¿Tiene una cinta?
sentences.english: Mine is blue and has a red ribbon. Does it have a ribbon?
sentences.speaker: Tilo

sentences.spanish: Tiene una cinta y una voz muy fuerte.
sentences.english: It has a ribbon and a very loud voice.
sentences.speaker: Pipa

continuation.spanish: Es mi teatro pequeño. Las marionetas tienen un concierto esta noche.
continuation.english: It’s my little theatre. The puppets have a concert tonight.
continuation.speaker: Tilo

continuation.spanish: Pues necesitan salir. Mi tren llega ahora.
continuation.english: Well, they need to get out. My train is arriving now.
continuation.speaker: Pipa

continuation.spanish: No tengo la llave. Está en el bolsillo de tu abrigo.
continuation.english: I don’t have the key. It’s in your coat pocket.
continuation.speaker: Tilo

continuation.spanish: Pipa mira su abrigo. Es demasiado grande y tiene tres bolsillos secretos.
continuation.english: Pipa looks at his coat. It is too big and has three secret pockets.
continuation.speaker: Narrador

ending.spanish: También llevo tu abrigo. Hoy no reconozco nada.
ending.english: I’m wearing your coat too. Today I don’t recognise anything.
ending.speaker: Pipa

ending.spanish: Tilo abre la maleta. Una marioneta se inclina ante los viajeros.
ending.english: Tilo opens the suitcase. A puppet bows to the travellers.
ending.speaker: Narrador

ending.spanish: Gracias por venir al concierto de la estación. La entrada es gratis.
ending.english: Thank you for coming to the station concert. Admission is free.
ending.speaker: Tilo

ending.spanish: Y ahora, por favor, ¿dónde está mi maleta?
ending.english: And now, please, where is my suitcase?
ending.speaker: Pipa

scene: Inside a station. Pipa waits with a blue suitcase. Something is singing inside.

author: Tilo
title: Una mesa para la luna
summary: Brasa’s restaurant receives a booking from a guest who cannot fit through the door.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Exterior del restaurante de Brasa. Hay tres platos sobre una mesa y una reserva sin nombre.
sentences.english: Outside Brasa’s restaurant. There are three plates on a table and a booking without a name.
sentences.speaker: Narrador

sentences.spanish: La reserva dice que llega después del atardecer y que necesita mucho espacio.
sentences.english: The booking says the guest arrives after sunset and needs plenty of room.
sentences.speaker: Brasa

sentences.spanish: Entonces no pongas la mesa junto a la puerta. Puede ser un gigante.
sentences.english: Then don’t put the table beside the door. It could be a giant.
sentences.speaker: Mora

sentences.spanish: He preparado sopa para tres. Un gigante necesita una olla entera.
sentences.english: I’ve made soup for three. A giant needs a whole pot.
sentences.speaker: Brasa

continuation.spanish: La luna aparece sobre el tejado. Una voz baja hasta la terraza.
continuation.english: The moon appears above the roof. A voice drifts down to the terrace.
continuation.speaker: Narrador

continuation.spanish: Buenas noches. Reservé una mesa porque siempre os veo cenar juntos.
continuation.english: Good evening. I booked a table because I always see you eating together.
continuation.speaker: Luna

continuation.spanish: No podemos subirte la sopa, pero podemos acercar la mesa al estanque.
continuation.english: We can’t bring the soup up to you, but we can move the table to the pond.
continuation.speaker: Mora

continuation.spanish: Allí hay sitio para tu reflejo. Espero que no tengas mucha hambre.
continuation.english: There’s room for your reflection there. I hope you aren’t very hungry.
continuation.speaker: Brasa

ending.spanish: Brasa y Mora cenan junto al agua. La luna tiembla en el tercer plato.
ending.english: Brasa and Mora dine beside the water. The moon trembles in the third plate.
ending.speaker: Narrador

ending.spanish: No quería comer. Quería saber de qué os reís cuando se apagan las luces.
ending.english: I didn’t want to eat. I wanted to know what you laugh about when the lights go out.
ending.speaker: Luna

ending.spanish: Esta noche nos reímos de un dragón que preparó sopa para el cielo.
ending.english: Tonight we’re laughing about a dragon who made soup for the sky.
ending.speaker: Brasa

ending.spanish: Los tres se ríen. Brasa deja la tercera silla fuera para la próxima noche despejada.
ending.english: All three laugh. Brasa leaves the third chair outside for the next clear night.
ending.speaker: Narrador

scene: Outside Brasa’s restaurant. There are three plates on a table and a booking without a name.

author: Tilo
title: El último ensayo
summary: An empty theatre becomes the setting for the performance Tilo least expected.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Interior de un teatro al borde del cierre. Tilo ensaya una despedida ante las butacas vacías.
sentences.english: Inside a theatre on the verge of closing. Tilo rehearses a farewell before the empty seats.
sentences.speaker: Narrador

sentences.spanish: «Cuando caiga el telón, nadie recordará nuestros nombres». No. Es demasiado triste.
sentences.english: “When the curtain falls, nobody will remember our names.” No. It’s too sad.
sentences.speaker: Tilo

sentences.spanish: Quizá deberías preguntar a quienes se sentaron aquí antes de decidir lo que recuerdan.
sentences.english: Perhaps you should ask the people who sat here before deciding what they remember.
sentences.speaker: Faro

sentences.spanish: Les invité al estreno. No vino nadie.
sentences.english: I invited them to the opening night. Nobody came.
sentences.speaker: Tilo

continuation.spanish: Faro abre una caja de invitaciones junto a la puerta. Todas llevan la fecha del día siguiente.
continuation.english: Faro opens a box of invitations beside the door. They all bear the following day’s date.
continuation.speaker: Narrador

continuation.spanish: Has confundido el ensayo con el estreno. Todavía tienes una noche.
continuation.english: You’ve mistaken the rehearsal for the opening night. You still have one night.
continuation.speaker: Faro

continuation.spanish: Una noche no basta para inventar un final que quiera escuchar.
continuation.english: One night isn’t enough to invent an ending I want to hear.
continuation.speaker: Tilo

continuation.spanish: Entonces cuenta por qué abriste este lugar. Esa historia ya la conoces.
continuation.english: Then tell them why you opened this place. You already know that story.
continuation.speaker: Faro

ending.spanish: La noche siguiente llegan vecinos con sillas porque las butacas no alcanzan. Tilo sale sin disfraz.
ending.english: The following evening, neighbours arrive with chairs because there are not enough seats. Tilo comes out without a costume.
ending.speaker: Narrador

ending.spanish: Abrí el teatro porque tenía miedo de hablar y necesitaba que alguien fingiera escucharme.
ending.english: I opened the theatre because I was afraid of speaking and needed someone to pretend to listen to me.
ending.speaker: Tilo

ending.spanish: Hoy no tenemos que fingir.
ending.english: Today we don’t have to pretend.
ending.speaker: Faro

ending.spanish: Tilo deja el guion en el suelo. El edificio cerrará el lunes; esa noche, sin embargo, aún les pertenece.
ending.english: Tilo puts the script on the floor. The building will close on Monday; that night, however, still belongs to them.
ending.speaker: Narrador

scene: Inside a theatre on the verge of closing. Tilo rehearses a farewell before the empty seats.

author: Mora
title: Ser: El retrato equivocado
summary: Mora’s portrait introduces someone she does not recognise. Practise identity and roles as she asks for a truer picture.

verbFocus.scope: Identity, relationships, and roles. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Mora llega al taller para recoger su retrato y encuentra una reina con corona.
sentences.english: Mora arrives at the workshop to collect her portrait and finds a queen wearing a crown.

sentences.spanish: «Soy Mora, pero esa reina no soy yo», dice la duendecilla.
sentences.english: “I am Mora, but that queen is not me,” says the sprite.

sentences.spanish: «Eres una duendecilla; pensé que necesitabas un castillo», responde el pintor.
sentences.english: “You are a sprite; I thought you needed a castle,” replies the painter.

sentences.spanish: «Mi casa es pequeña y mi mejor amiga es una polilla», explica ella.
sentences.english: “My home is small and my best friend is a moth,” she explains.

sentences.spanish: «Somos compañeras de aventuras; esas damas del cuadro son otras personas».
sentences.english: “We are adventure companions; those ladies in the painting are other people.”

sentences.spanish: El pintor mira a Mora y a Luma: «Entonces, ¿sois exploradoras?».
sentences.english: The painter looks at Mora and Luma: “Then, are you explorers?”

continuation.spanish: «Mis zapatos son viejos porque camino mucho», contesta Mora, mostrando el barro.
continuation.english: “My shoes are old because I walk a lot,” answers Mora, showing the mud.

continuation.spanish: Luma añade: «Ella es quien escucha cuando todos hablan a la vez».
continuation.english: Luma adds, “She is the one who listens when everyone speaks at once.”

continuation.spanish: «Y tú eres quien encuentra luz en los lugares oscuros», responde Mora.
continuation.english: “And you are the one who finds light in dark places,” replies Mora.

continuation.spanish: El pintor baja el pincel: «Soy bueno pintando coronas, pero no os conozco».
continuation.english: The painter lowers his brush: “I am good at painting crowns, but I don’t know you.”

continuation.spanish: Mora le ofrece una silla: «Somos tres; podemos compartir el almuerzo».
continuation.english: Mora offers him a chair: “There are three of us; we can share lunch.”

continuation.spanish: Mientras comen, el pintor escucha sus aventuras: «Sois muy valientes», dice al final.
continuation.english: As they eat, the painter listens to their adventures: “You are very brave,” he says at the end.

ending.spanish: Al final de la tarde enseña un dibujo nuevo, sin castillo ni corona.
ending.english: At the end of the afternoon he shows them a new drawing, without a castle or a crown.

ending.spanish: «Sois vosotras, tal como os veo ahora», dice con un poco de miedo.
ending.english: “It is you, just as I see you now,” he says a little nervously.

ending.spanish: «Somos nosotras después de cruzar el río», dice Luma; «y tú eres quien nos ha escuchado».
ending.english: “It is us after crossing the river,” says Luma, “and you are the one who listened to us.”

ending.spanish: «Estas son nuestras caras después de una aventura», dice Luma, riendo.
ending.english: “These are our faces after an adventure,” says Luma, laughing.

ending.spanish: Mora mira sus zapatos embarrados en el papel: «Sí, esa soy yo».
ending.english: Mora looks at her muddy shoes on the paper: “Yes, that is me.”

ending.spanish: El retrato es pequeño, pero Mora encuentra un lugar para él bajo su seta.
ending.english: The portrait is small, but Mora finds a place for it beneath her mushroom.

author: Mora
title: Estar: La puerta del camerino
summary: Just before the show, Mora discovers that the smallest performer is missing. Practise location and temporary states in a backstage rescue.

verbFocus.scope: Location and how someone feels or is doing. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Faltan diez minutos para la función y Mora está detrás del escenario.
sentences.english: There are ten minutes until the performance, and Mora is behind the stage.

sentences.spanish: «Estoy lista», dice, pero oye un golpe dentro del camerino.
sentences.english: “I’m ready,” she says, but she hears a knock inside the dressing room.

sentences.spanish: «¿Estás ahí, Benji?», pregunta junto a la puerta cerrada.
sentences.english: “Are you there, Benji?” she asks beside the locked door.

sentences.spanish: «Estoy aquí y la llave está fuera», responde el ratón.
sentences.english: “I’m here, and the key is outside,” replies the mouse.

sentences.spanish: Tilo llega con Faro: «Estamos buscando la llave desde hace media hora».
sentences.english: Tilo arrives with Faro: “We’ve been looking for the key for half an hour.”

sentences.spanish: «¿Estáis seguros? ¿Dónde están vuestros abrigos?», pregunta Mora.
sentences.english: “Are you sure? Where are your coats?” asks Mora.

continuation.spanish: Los bolsillos están vacíos, pero el abrigo de Tilo está colgado al otro lado.
continuation.english: The pockets are empty, but Tilo’s coat is hanging on the other side.

continuation.spanish: «Estoy seguro: la llave está en mi abrigo», recuerda Tilo, tapándose la cara.
continuation.english: “I’m sure: the key is in my coat,” Tilo remembers, covering his face.

continuation.spanish: Benji alcanza el abrigo, pero la cerradura está demasiado alta para él.
continuation.english: Benji reaches the coat, but the lock is too high for him.

continuation.spanish: «Estamos cerca de resolverlo», dice Mora, y pasa una cinta por debajo de la puerta.
continuation.english: “We’re close to solving it,” says Mora, and she passes a ribbon under the door.

continuation.spanish: «Si estás junto al suelo, ata la llave a esta cinta».
continuation.english: “If you’re down by the floor, tie the key to this ribbon.”

continuation.spanish: Faro pregunta a Tilo: «¿Estáis preparados para retrasar la función un momento?».
continuation.english: Faro asks Tilo, “Are you all prepared to delay the performance for a moment?”

ending.spanish: «Los músicos están avisados», responde Tilo mientras Mora tira despacio de la cinta.
ending.english: “The musicians have been told,” replies Tilo as Mora slowly pulls the ribbon.

ending.spanish: La llave pasa por debajo de la puerta y Benji sale con las orejas torcidas.
ending.english: The key passes under the door, and Benji comes out with his ears bent.

ending.spanish: «Estoy bien, pero necesito agua», dice el ratón.
ending.english: “I’m fine, but I need water,” says the mouse.

ending.spanish: Mora le trae un vaso: «Estás a salvo; estamos aquí contigo».
ending.english: Mora brings him a glass: “You’re safe; we’re here with you.”

ending.spanish: «¿Estáis listos?», pregunta Tilo; todos están en sus puestos y empieza la música.
ending.english: “Are you ready?” asks Tilo; everyone is in position and the music begins.

ending.spanish: Benji deja la llave en un clavo bajo: esta vez está a su alcance.
ending.english: Benji leaves the key on a low nail: this time it is within his reach.

author: Mora
title: Querer: Dos caminos
summary: Mora and Pipa want different journeys. Practise expressing wishes as they plan a farewell without treating it as a failure.

verbFocus.scope: Wants, wishes, and affection. Six present-indicative forms; vosotros is used in Spain.

license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Pipa ha comprado un billete hacia el sur, pero todavía no se lo ha dicho a Mora.
sentences.english: Pipa has bought a ticket south, but he has not told Mora yet.

sentences.spanish: «Quiero enseñarte algo», dice al dejarlo sobre la mesa del desayuno.
sentences.english: “I want to show you something,” he says as he puts it on the breakfast table.

sentences.spanish: Mora lee la fecha: «¿Quieres marcharte esta misma semana?».
sentences.english: Mora reads the date: “Do you want to leave this very week?”

sentences.spanish: «Mi hermana quiere que la ayude en su taller antes del invierno».
sentences.english: “My sister wants me to help her in her workshop before winter.”

sentences.spanish: «¿Ya no queremos cruzar las montañas juntos? Los demás quieren saberlo», responde Mora.
sentences.english: “Don’t we want to cross the mountains together any more? The others want to know,” replies Mora.

sentences.spanish: Luma deja dos tazas frente a ellos: «Si queréis, puedo daros un momento a solas».
sentences.english: Luma puts two cups in front of them: “If you want, I can give you a moment alone.”

continuation.spanish: «Nuestros amigos quieren despedirse, pero no saben si habrá viaje», explica Pipa.
continuation.english: “Our friends want to say goodbye, but they don’t know whether there will be a trip,” explains Pipa.

continuation.spanish: Mora admite que no quiere acompañarlo al sur; lleva meses preparando el camino de montaña.
continuation.english: Mora admits that she does not want to accompany him south; she has been preparing the mountain route for months.

continuation.spanish: «Te quiero, pero también quiero hacer este viaje», añade la duendecilla.
continuation.english: “I love you, but I also want to make this journey,” adds the sprite.

continuation.spanish: Pipa asiente: «No quiero que renuncies a él para evitar una despedida».
continuation.english: Pipa nods: “I don’t want you to give it up to avoid a goodbye.”

continuation.spanish: «Entonces queremos cosas distintas, aunque sigamos siendo amigos».
continuation.english: “Then we want different things, even though we are still friends.”

continuation.spanish: Luma vuelve: «¿Queréis que os ayude? Mora, ¿quieres que lleve tus mapas?».
continuation.english: Luma returns: “Would you like me to help? Mora, would you like me to carry your maps?”

ending.spanish: La noche anterior a la salida, Luma pregunta: «¿Queréis cenar aquí o junto al río?».
ending.english: The night before departure, Luma asks, “Do you want to eat here or beside the river?”

ending.spanish: «Queremos ir al río», dice Pipa; Mora quiere llevar los mapas y todos quieren verlos.
ending.english: “We want to go to the river,” says Pipa; Mora wants to bring the maps, and everyone wants to see them.

ending.spanish: Mora le pide a Pipa que le escriba cuando llegue: «Quiero saber cómo es el taller».
ending.english: Mora asks Pipa to write when he arrives: “I want to know what the workshop is like.”

ending.spanish: «Si quieres, puedo enviarte dibujos; yo quiero ver tus montañas», responde él.
ending.english: “If you want, I can send you drawings; I want to see your mountains,” he replies.

ending.spanish: A la mañana siguiente se separan en el cruce, sin fingir que no les duele.
ending.english: The next morning they part at the crossroads, without pretending it does not hurt.

ending.spanish: Cada uno lleva una taza que el otro ha elegido para el camino.
ending.english: Each carries a cup that the other has chosen for the journey.

author: Faro
title: La cena sobre el canal
summary: In Bangkok, Faro follows the smell of dinner to a table that has no spare chairs.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: Faro llegó a Bangkok al anochecer, cuando él empezaba a sentirse despierto.
sentences.english: Faro arrived in Bangkok at dusk, just as he was starting to feel awake.

sentences.spanish: Desde un puente vio una mesa sobre el canal y olió una sopa que le recordó el granero.
sentences.english: From a bridge he saw a table above the canal and smelled a soup that reminded him of the barn.

sentences.spanish: Bajó para preguntar si podía cenar, pero todas las sillas estaban ocupadas.
sentences.english: He went down to ask whether he could eat, but every chair was taken.

sentences.spanish: La cocinera señaló una caja y le pidió que esperara.
sentences.english: The cook pointed to a box and asked him to wait.

continuation.spanish: Faro creyó que debía sentarse allí, hasta que la caja empezó a moverse.
continuation.english: Faro thought he was meant to sit there, until the box began to move.

continuation.spanish: Dentro había platos que la cocinera necesitaba llevar a sus vecinos al otro lado del puente.
continuation.english: Inside were dishes the cook needed to take to her neighbours on the other side of the bridge.

continuation.spanish: El búho se ofreció a vigilar la caja mientras ella buscaba un carro.
continuation.english: The owl offered to watch the box while she fetched a cart.

continuation.spanish: Una lluvia repentina llenó el patio, y Faro extendió las alas sobre los platos.
continuation.english: A sudden shower filled the courtyard, and Faro spread his wings over the dishes.

ending.spanish: Entre todos llevaron la cena al otro lado y juntaron varias mesas bajo un tejado.
ending.english: Together they carried dinner across and pushed several tables together under a roof.

ending.spanish: Esta vez hubo sitio para Faro, aunque sus plumas mojadas ocuparon dos sillas.
ending.english: This time there was room for Faro, although his wet feathers took up two chairs.

ending.spanish: Escuchó historias del barrio hasta muy tarde y pidió permiso para escribir una de ellas.
ending.english: He listened to neighbourhood stories until very late and asked permission to write one of them down.

ending.spanish: Al marcharse, la cocinera le dio sopa para el camino y una toalla que debía devolver.
ending.english: When he left, the cook gave him soup for the journey and a towel he had to return.

author: Faro
title: El farol de la playa
summary: A quiet beach walk leads Faro to a fisherman searching for a message he cannot replace.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: En Pattaya, Faro dejó atrás la música de una calle y caminó hacia una parte tranquila de la playa.
sentences.english: In Pattaya, Faro left the music of a street behind and walked towards a quiet stretch of beach.

sentences.spanish: Allí vio a un pescador que buscaba algo con un farol casi apagado.
sentences.english: There he saw a fisherman searching for something with an almost extinguished lantern.

sentences.spanish: Había perdido una pequeña botella mientras sacaba las redes.
sentences.english: He had lost a small bottle while bringing in the nets.

sentences.spanish: Faro ofreció sus ojos de búho; el hombre solo tenía que explicar qué debía buscar.
sentences.english: Faro offered his owl’s eyes; the man only had to explain what to look for.

continuation.spanish: La botella llevaba dentro una carta de su hija, que vivía lejos.
continuation.english: The bottle contained a letter from his daughter, who lived far away.

continuation.spanish: No era un mensaje arrojado al mar: el pescador la usaba para proteger el papel del agua.
continuation.english: It was not a message thrown into the sea: the fisherman used it to protect the paper from water.

continuation.spanish: Faro voló sobre la orilla y vio un reflejo entre unas cuerdas abandonadas.
continuation.english: Faro flew over the shore and saw a reflection among some abandoned ropes.

continuation.spanish: Aterrizó justo antes de que una ola arrastrara la botella.
continuation.english: He landed just before a wave could carry the bottle away.

ending.spanish: El hombre abrió la carta con cuidado y leyó que su hija volvería al mes siguiente.
ending.english: The man carefully opened the letter and read that his daughter would return the following month.

ending.spanish: Faro lo ayudó a recoger las cuerdas para que no quedaran en la playa.
ending.english: Faro helped him collect the ropes so they would not remain on the beach.

ending.spanish: Después compartieron té, mientras la música seguía sonando a lo lejos.
ending.english: Afterwards they shared tea while the music continued in the distance.

ending.spanish: El búho apuntó la fecha de la visita en su cuaderno, por si todavía andaba cerca.
ending.english: The owl noted the date of the visit in his notebook, in case he was still nearby.

author: Faro
title: La toalla y el billete
summary: Before leaving Thailand, Faro has one small promise to keep and very little time to keep it.
license: Original fictional Cuentiva editorial edition. Native-speaker editorial review pending.

sentences.spanish: La última mañana de su viaje, Faro encontró una toalla doblada en el fondo de la mochila.
sentences.english: On the last morning of his trip, Faro found a folded towel at the bottom of his backpack.

sentences.spanish: Era de la cocinera que lo había recibido en Bangkok durante la lluvia.
sentences.english: It belonged to the cook who had welcomed him in Bangkok during the rain.

sentences.spanish: Su tren salía en dos horas y el restaurante estaba al otro lado de la ciudad.
sentences.english: His train left in two hours, and the restaurant was on the other side of the city.

sentences.spanish: El búho podía enviarla después, pero recordaba que había prometido volver.
sentences.english: The owl could send it later, but he remembered that he had promised to return.

continuation.spanish: Pidió ayuda para encontrar el camino más rápido y llegó con las plumas revueltas.
continuation.english: He asked for help finding the fastest route and arrived with his feathers ruffled.

continuation.spanish: El restaurante estaba cerrado, aunque se oían voces en el piso de arriba.
continuation.english: The restaurant was closed, although voices could be heard upstairs.

continuation.spanish: La cocinera abrió una ventana: estaban preparando una comida familiar.
continuation.english: The cook opened a window: they were preparing a family meal.

continuation.spanish: Faro levantó la toalla y el billete, sin saber cómo explicar tanta prisa.
continuation.english: Faro held up the towel and the ticket, unsure how to explain such a hurry.

ending.spanish: Ella bajó, recogió la toalla y le puso un paquete de comida en las manos.
ending.english: She came down, took the towel and put a food parcel in his hands.

ending.spanish: Su nieto lo acompañó hasta la estación por un camino que Faro no conocía.
ending.english: Her grandson accompanied him to the station along a route Faro did not know.

ending.spanish: Al subir al tren, el búho abrió el paquete y encontró una nota: «La próxima vez, sin prisa».
ending.english: As he boarded the train, the owl opened the parcel and found a note: “Next time, no rushing.”

ending.spanish: Faro guardó la nota en el lugar de la toalla y empezó a escribir el viaje de vuelta.
ending.english: Faro put the note where the towel had been and began to write about the journey home.
